두 자매의 집이 집회 장소로 사용되었죠.
1세기와 마찬가지로 20세기에도 이곳의 형제 자매들은 심한 반대를 받았습니다.
파시스트 정부와 교직자들은 여호와의 증인의 활동을 중단시키려고 수십 년 동안 노력했습니다.
하지만 우리의 형제들은 인내했죠.
예를 들어 1925년에 이 호텔에서 최초의 순회 대회가 열렸는데
형제들은 의심을 피하기 위해 결혼식도 같이 열었습니다.
실제로 이 대회 중에 레미조 쿠미네티 형제와 알비나 프로티 자매가 결혼식을 올렸죠.
현재 이탈리아 지부는 25만 명이 넘는 전도인들을 지원하고 있습니다.
이탈리아뿐 아니라 이탈리아 안에 있는 작은 국가인 산마리노 공화국의 활동도 감독하고 있죠.
형제 자매들은 알베로벨로 같은 오래된 마을에서도 전파하는데,
이 마을은 석회암으로 만든 트룰리라는 집으로 유명합니다.
또 유명한 도시들에서 공개 증거도 합니다.
피렌체나 베니스 같은 도시들이 있죠.
2023년에는 특별한 봉사가 조직되었는데요.
로마와 밀라노에 있는 회중의 전파 활동을 지원하기 위해
인근 회중의 전도인들이 주말에 그 두 도시에 가서 함께 봉사했습니다.
거의 1만 3000명의 전도인이 참여했고 63건의 연구가 시작되었죠!
이탈리아에는 난민들이 많은데요.
아프리카, 아시아, 동유럽에서 온 사람들이죠.
난민들에게 전파하는 일을 돕기 위해 이탈리아 지부는 35개 언어로
420개의 언어 학습 과정을 마련했습니다.
그중에는 암하라어, 신할리즈어, 트위어, 우크라이나어가 있죠.
이탈리아에 대해 말하면서 음식 얘기를 빼놓을 순 없죠.
이탈리아 사람들은 맛있는 음식을 먹는 것을 좋아하고 음식을 중요하게 생각합니다.
이탈리아는 다양한 와인으로 유명하고 지역마다 유명한 음식들이 있습니다.
피자와 파스타 그리고 파르메산 치즈와 손으로 만든 모차렐라 치즈가 있죠.
피네롤로 수드 회중의 형제 자매들이 따뜻한 사랑과 인사를 전합니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다!

en.text: Welcome to the December 2024 edition
of JW Broadcasting®!
The 140th annual meeting
of the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society
of Pennsylvania
was held on October 5, 2024.
The program featured encouraging spiritual talks and videos.
Please enjoy the first part of the annual meeting!
So, what an eventful year it has been!
As expressed at Psalm 65:11,
Jehovah has indeed ‘crowned the year with goodness’
in a spiritual sense.
Since our last annual meeting, Jehovah has directed his people
in many different ways, reflecting his love and wisdom.
Of course, the most significant occurrence
is that we’ve welcomed back thousands
who had been removed from the congregation.
And certainly there has been great “joy in heaven”
but here on earth as well.
We’re delighted to have these dear ones
back with us once again, wouldn’t you agree?
Also, we were thrilled by this year’s conventions
featuring The Good News According to Jesus,
as we saw in the video prelude.
And we just completed a global campaign to start Bible studies.
We see the growth that’s taking place in the field.
And in other news, there’s a new product in the Bethel commissary—beard butter,
not to be confused with the butter that you spread on your toast.
Yes, adjustments to our dress and grooming were also a highlight of the year.
Additionally, less than a year ago, the PVC opened for tours,
not to be confused with polyvinyl chloride
for all you plumbers out there.
No, we’re talking about the PVC, the Patterson Visitors’ Center.
Here’s an experience from the first-century village.
A young girl was very impressed by the village
and was trying to just understand, or comprehend,
what she was seeing around her.
She noticed all the costumed attendants walking around
demonstrating trades or just speaking with the visitors.
She asked her mother, “Are these resurrected ones?”
A young boy about ten was with his family
and enjoyed seeing a brother in costume demonstrating the winepress.
Well, the family continued walking through the marketplace
and then into the courtyard, but the little boy kept coming back.
He kept coming back to the winepress,
and the costumed attendant told him, “You must really enjoy it here.”
And he said, “Yes!”
Then the boy paused, and he said, “I’m from the future.”
He went on to show his phone to the attendant and show how he has the Bible on it.
The attendant explained
he’d seen others come through the village with such devices,
but he only reads Hebrew.
The young brother looked at him and said,
“I have the Bible in many languages.”
So the young brother put himself into the spirit of the time period
and was quite affected by the impact of the Bible village.
So no doubt you too will enjoy your tour, if you haven’t already gone.
Even if it’s a return visit, you’ll still be delighted
to see people from the first century.
Now, in years gone by, Brother Russell Kurzen
(many of you remember him)
was sort of like the Bethel historian because he would relate
specific events that occurred on that day
to the Morning Worship chairman, who often would share them then with the Bethel family.
Well, today is October 5,
so put on your thinking caps for a moment.
What noteworthy events in history
have occurred on October 5?
Does “MENE, MENE, TEKEL, and PARSIN” ring a bell?
Yes, the handwriting on the wall appeared in Belshazzar’s palace
on October 5, 539 B.C.E.,
according to the Gregorian calendar.
But what about in our Common Era?
In the month of October 1924,
Jehovah’s people were busy distributing around the world
a printed resolution entitled
Ecclesiastics Indicted.
Now, this is a copy of that tract, life-size.
Imagine distributing this tract to people in your territory
or putting it in their doors.
The introduction to the resolution stated the following:
“The indictment herein is laid chiefly against the clergy,
“showing that they have fallen before the temptations of Satan,
“proved unfaithful to the Lord and to the responsibility resting upon them;
“and that this is the chief cause
of the world’s present deplorable state”
—strong words from the organization back in 1924.
Point number three of the resolution stated this:
“That they [the clergy] have failed and refused to preach to the people
“the message of Messiah’s kingdom
“and to point them to the evidences relating to his second coming;
“and being unwilling to await the Lord’s due time to set up His kingdom
“and being ambitious to appear wise and great,
“they have, together with their co-conspirators,
“claimed the ability to set up God’s kingdom on earth without God,
“and have endorsed the League of Nations and declared it to be
“‘the political expression of God’s kingdom on earth,’
“thereby breaking their allegiance to the Lord Jesus Christ
“and declaring their allegiance to the devil, the god of evil;
“and to this end they have advocated and sanctified war,
“turned their church edifices into recruiting stations
“[does that sound like any of the churches in modern times?],
“acted as recruiting officers for pay,
“and preached men into the trenches, there to suffer and die”
—quite a resolution—
Ecclesiastics Indicted.
Nothing has changed.
The clergy still teach lies, foment war, and fail to preach the good news.
They’re still riding on the back of the beast too.
Well, back in 1924, as reported
in the October 2024 study edition of The Watchtower:
‘In the small town of Cleveland, Oklahoma,
‘Brother Frank Johnson
‘finished distributing the tracts
‘20 minutes before he was to be picked up by other publishers.
‘Well, he couldn’t just wait out in the open because men from the town
‘were angered and they were seeking to find him.
‘So Brother Johnson decided to hide in a nearby church.
‘Finding it empty,
‘he left copies of Ecclesiastics Indicted
‘in the preacher’s Bible and at each seat.
‘He exited the church as quickly as he had come.
‘Well, he still had some time, so he visited two more churches,
‘following a similar pattern.
‘Frank rushed back to the spot where he was to be picked up.
‘He hid behind a fuel station,
‘keeping an eye out for the men who were after him.
‘The men drove by, but they didn’t see him.
‘As soon as they were gone, Frank’s fellow preachers,
‘who had been witnessing nearby, arrived to pick him up,
‘and they all drove off together.
‘Now, as they were leaving town,
‘one of the brothers recalled:
‘“We passed by the three churches.
‘“There were as many as 50 people standing out in front of each church.
‘“Some of the people were reading the tract,
‘“others were holding it up for the preacher to see.
‘“Well, we had a very close call!”
‘He said: “But we thanked Jehovah our God for his protection
and the knowledge to outwit these enemies of the Kingdom.”’
So that’s part of our theocratic history, your theocratic history.
You continue to preach with the same boldness.
Those were exciting times,
but we too are living in exciting times.
On October 5, 2002,
it was announced at the annual meeting that printing operations in the United States
would be moved from Brooklyn to Wallkill.
Amazing!
On October 5, 2013, what happened?
Likely you recall, Brother Jackson
released the revised New World Translation in English.
Amazing!
On October 5, 2019, what happened?
The Ramapo project was announced.
Amazing!
Jehovah continues to bless his organization.
Well, what will we hear today?
Calls to action?
Kind reminders?
Exciting announcements?
Praise to Jehovah?
Absolutely!
And a few surprises along the way.
So don’t change the channel.
Ten years ago at the annual meeting of 2014,
we were introduced to the first epic episode
of the series Become Jehovah’s Friend.
And it was entitled Jehovah Will Help You Be Bold.
Since that time, five additional epic episodes have been released,
including Make Jehovah Happy,
Jehovah Forgives, Does Jehovah Answer Prayers?,
Who Should Be My Friend?, and  You Are Precious to Jehovah.
How these videos have helped our young ones and really all of us
to visualize Bible accounts and heavenly realities!
Well, we’re happy to inform you that another epic episode
will soon be ready for release but not just yet.
But we can show you the trailer to increase anticipation.
It’s entitled Become Jehovah’s Friend —The Greatest Act of Love.
Let’s watch.
I miss her so much.
Hey!
Soon, we’re having the Memorial,
and you have to come!
It’s the most important event.
He loves all of us.
He loves you.
Soon, Jesus will resurrect people,
and because he died for us, we can all live forever!
It’s the greatest gift anyone could give us.
Mom!
Should we get ready for the Memorial?
Let’s do it!
Yay!
As we all go home tonight,
think about what Jesus’ sacrifice
means to you.
Certainly, we anticipate the release of the full-length episode.
Well, the next part of our program
is a symposium from three members of the Governing Body.
Each speaker will introduce the next.
But the first talk of our symposium
will be given by the longest-serving member of the Governing Body, Brother Gerrit Lösch.
This past July, he completed 30 years of serving on the Governing Body.
Brother Lösch will now discuss the theme “Our Privilege to Glorify Jehovah.”
As you can see, this is a mirror.
Did you look into a mirror before you came here?
Perhaps judging by your neat and clean appearance,
you obviously did.
Ancient mirrors were generally made of metal,
such as bronze or copper and even silver and gold.
They had to be highly polished
but still did not have finely reflecting surfaces
as do glass mirrors.
This is why the apostle Paul said at 1 Corinthians 13:12:
“For now we see in hazy outline
by means of a metal mirror.”
Probably only in the first century
were glass mirrors introduced.
In the Scriptures, we find two figurative uses
of the term “mirror.”
For instance, at James chapter 1
verses 22-25, it says:
“However, become doers of the word and not hearers only,
“deceiving yourselves with false reasoning.
“For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer,
“this one is like a man looking at his own face in a mirror.
“For he looks at himself, and he goes away
“and immediately forgets what sort of person he is.
“But the one who peers
“into the perfect law that belongs to freedom
“and continues in it
“has become, not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work;
and he will be happy in what he does.”
And the apostle Paul
showed that Christians reflect like mirrors
the glory of Jehovah in their ministry.
In 2 Corinthians chapter 3,
he wrote at chapter 3 and verse 18:
“And all of us,
“while we with unveiled faces
“reflect like mirrors the glory of Jehovah,
“are transformed into the same image
“from one degree of glory to another,
exactly as it is done by Jehovah the Spirit.”
And in chapter 4, verse 1, he says:
“Therefore, since we have this ministry
through the mercy that was shown us, we do not give up.”
So God’s Word is compared to a mirror
that we can use to examine ourselves.
On the other hand, Christians themselves
are also compared to a mirror
—a mirror that reflects Jehovah’s glory.
So how do the Scriptures use the word “glory”?
Well, there are different types of glory.
At 1 Corinthians chapter 15,
verses 40-44, it says:
“And there are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies;
“but the glory of the heavenly bodies is one sort,
“and that of the earthly bodies is a different sort.
“The glory of the sun is one sort,
“and the glory of the moon is another,
“and the glory of the stars is another;
“in fact, one star differs from another star in glory.
“So it is with the resurrection of the dead.
“It is sown in corruption; it is raised up in incorruption.
“It is sown in dishonor; it is raised up in glory.
“It is sown in weakness; it is raised up in power.
It is sown a physical body; it is raised up a spiritual body.”
Now, let’s discuss five types of glory.
Of course, Jehovah has and deserves
the highest degree of glory.
Then there’s the glory of Jesus,
which is second to the one of God.
At John 1:14, it says:
“So the Word became flesh and resided among us,
“and we had a view of his glory,
“a glory such as belongs
“to an only-begotten son from a father;
and he was full of divine favor and truth.”
—John 1:14.
The Bible shows that Jesus was given more glory after his resurrection
than he had before he came to the earth.
It says: “Jesus, who was made
“a little lower than angels,
“now crowned with glory and honor
for having suffered death.”
—Hebrews 2:9.
The third point:
Annointed Christians also have a measure of glory.
Jude verse 8 says
that in the first century there were some who
were “speaking abusively of glorious ones.”
Who were the “glorious ones” in the first century?
Anointed overseers.
They had a measure of glory when they lived on earth.
Number four: When taken to heaven, all anointed,
not only anointed overseers, will receive everlasting glory.
Second Timothy 2:10 says:
“For this reason I go on enduring all things
“for the sake of the chosen ones,
“so that they too may obtain the salvation that is through Christ Jesus,
along with everlasting glory.”
But we have today not a few but many glorious ones,
even sitting in the audience right here.
How so?
Because the expression “glorious ones”
refers also to elders with an earthly hope.
The Watchtower, 1997,
September 1, page 16,
paragraph 14 says:
“Christian elders represent
“the glorious Jehovah God and his Son
“and, as a result, have certain glory
“conferred upon them.
“True, they make mistakes, as did Peter himself,
“but the Scriptures urge members of the congregation
to be submissive to such glorious ones.”
(End of quote)
And number five:
There’s the glorious good news.
No matter what hope we have,
we glorify Jehovah through our preaching and teaching.
Second Corinthians 4:3, 4 says:
“In fact, the good news we declare is veiled,
“it is veiled among those who are perishing,
“among whom the god of this system of things
“has blinded the minds of the unbelievers,
“so that the illumination of the glorious good news
about the Christ . . . might not shine through.”
How can we all glorify Jehovah?
Not only overseers and other adults in the congregation
reflect Jehovah’s glory
but also children can do so.
Children, are you aware of it?
You too!
Yes, we all can glorify Jehovah.
How?
In at least six ways.
Starting with point one,
we glorify him through our prayers
and then also by singing Kingdom songs.
Another point,
we glorify him by accumulating accurate knowledge.
Second Corinthians 4:6, therefore, says:
“For God is the one who said: ‘Let the light shine out of darkness,’
“and he has shone on our hearts to illuminate them
with the glorious knowledge of God by the face of Christ.”
Further, we glorify Jehovah by our Christian conduct.
Yes, we absorb this light of glorious knowledge of God
and transform our lives according to it.
It brings glory to Jehovah God.
One’s conduct can also cause others to give glory to God.
Our conduct is not perfect. We all know that.
Still, Jehovah accepts us.
However, that does not excuse us from keeping ourselves as mirrors
in a clean and polished shape as much as we can.
In the dark, no mirror reflects anything
except darkness.
The mirror does not have any glory or light in itself.
Similarly, we are aware that any glory we might have
is just a reflection of God’s glory.
First Peter 2:12 says:
“Maintain your conduct fine among the nations,
“so that when they accuse you of being wrongdoers,
“they may be eyewitnesses of your fine works
“and, as a result, glorify God
in the day of his inspection.”
Further, we glorify him
by doing good to others.
At Matthew 5:16, in the Sermon on the Mount,
Jesus himself showed that preaching and teaching is not enough.
We need to do good things to others aside from it.
We need to love our neighbors, including those at our workplace.
This may prompt people who are not Witnesses of Jehovah
to glorify God.
As Jesus put it (I quote):
“Let your light shine before men,
“so that they may see your fine works
“[so it’s not just preaching but fine works]
and give glory to your Father who is in the heavens.”
What’s another way
we all can reflect the glory of Jehovah like mirrors?
We glorify him by our preaching and teaching.
We want to conduct many Bible studies,
and we want to impart
“the glorious knowledge of God” to others.
“For God is the one who said: ‘Let the light shine out of darkness,’
and he has shone on our hearts to illuminate them,”
says Paul at 2 Corinthians 4:6.
And he continues:
“Illuminate them with the glorious knowledge of God
by the face of Christ.”
Many of us who are older have had the privilege
of reflecting the glory of Jehovah
for perhaps decades.
Jehovah has allowed us not only the privilege
of proclaiming the message of the Kingdom
but also some have served as elders, pioneers,
missionaries, Bethelites, construction servants,
circuit overseers, or Branch Committee members.
These are ways that we have reflected
the glory of Jehovah.
What a privilege we’ve had to do so, haven’t we?
In spite of all these privileges, we maintain a humble spirit.
We appreciate that the privileges we have enjoyed
are an undeserved kindness from Jehovah.
Having enjoyed so many privileges,
what unique responsibility do we as older ones now have?
We must allow the next generation to come up
so that they too can enjoy
unique privileges in glorifying Jehovah.
They are the next generation of circuit overseers,
Bethelites, missionaries,
construction servants, Branch Committee members, and so on.
We want them to have the marvelous privilege
that we have enjoyed as well.
That means we must look for ways
to teach them, to train them, to encourage them
so that they may use their youth and strength
and ability to glorify Jehovah.
What a privilege we have as older ones
to train and teach younger ones!
With that in mind, it is a pleasure to announce
that two additional brothers
have been appointed to serve as members of the Governing Body.
Well, Brothers Jody Jedele and Jacob Rumph
—both brothers are anointed Christians
who have a long history of loyal service to Jehovah.
Brother Jedele began his full-time service in 1989
and Bethel service in 1990.
Brother Rumph began his full-time service in 1995
and Bethel service in 2020.
Both brothers served as helpers
to the Service Committee of the Governing Body for a while.
We thank our heavenly Father, Jehovah,
for raising up such faithful men
to share in the work of the Governing Body.
We pray that Jehovah will richly bless
Brothers Jedele and Rumph and their wives.
We all worship our glorious God, Jehovah.
We have the glorious good news to spread.
Our whole life is for the glory of his praise.
Paul wrote at 1 Corinthians 10:31:
“Whether you are eating or drinking
“or doing anything else,
do all things for God’s glory.”
Will you endeavor to reflect like a mirror Jehovah’s glory
by making the truth manifest in word and example?
What a privilege!
At the end of the Millennium,
faithful ones on earth will receive and display a measure of glory
as perfect sons and daughters of Jehovah.
It says at Romans 8:21:
“The creation itself will also be set free
“from enslavement to corruption
and have the glorious freedom of the children of God.”
So keep polishing that mirror.
Look at the mirror of God’s Word every day.
And like a mirror, reflect God’s glory
by what you say and do.
Appreciate your privilege to glorify Jehovah God.
Help young ones to take on privileges of service.
We trust you will,
and we wish you Jehovah’s rich blessing in this endeavor.
So keep polishing and keep reflecting the light.
But how can you, our young ones,
glorify Jehovah by serving,
for instance, at Bethel and in theocratic construction?
What opportunities are available
for younger ones today?
For the answers to these questions,
let us now give our attention
to Brother Jeffrey Winder, a member of the Governing Body,
who will share the next talk in this symposium entitled
“Opportunities to Glorify Jehovah
at Bethel and in Theocratic Construction.”
Over 2,700 years ago,
Jehovah God inspired the faithful man Isaiah
to utter a prophecy that you and I are seeing fulfilled
before our eyes.
It’s found in Isaiah chapter 60.
I invite you to turn there with me.
Isaiah 60
—and let’s read together verse 22.
That verse says: “The little one will become a thousand
“and the small one a mighty nation.
“I myself, Jehovah,
will speed it up in its own time.”
Like passengers in a car that is increasing in speed,
do you sense the momentum
of what Jehovah’s organization is doing today?
Jehovah is accomplishing a tremendous work worldwide
all in connection with the Kingdom preaching work.
And in the face of Satanic attack and the wickedness of the last days,
what Jehovah is accomplishing truly glorifies his name.
But because so much work is being done,
there is a need for more workers to keep up with this work.
And in this talk, we’re specifically going to talk
about the needs at Bethel and in theocratic construction.
Well, what is the need?
In Bethel, we have a constant need
for spiritually qualified men and women
who can help carry the load of the ever-increasing and complex work.
And there is a particular need
for young brothers who can apply to come to Bethel
and be trained and in time qualify to serve as overseers
or to take the lead in departments such as the Service Department,
Public Information Department, Hospital Information Department,
and many others.
We need brothers who can in time qualify to serve
on Branch Committees.
And even in branches where the Bethel family is small,
we need young brothers to apply
because the brothers and sisters who have been carrying the load for years—
We love them, but they’re getting older.
And they have a zeal for the work,
but they recognize the need to train others
so that Jehovah’s work can continue.
And what about theocratic construction?
Well, there, too, there continues to be a need
for spiritually qualified men and women
who can help carry the tremendous amount of work
that is taking place in facility construction worldwide.
And there, too, we need spiritually qualified men
who can be trained in time to take the lead as trade overseers,
to serve as construction committee members,
and care for other assignments.
But how much work is there to do in theocratic construction?
Just to give you a glimpse,
consider some of the needs for Kingdom Halls
in a few countries in Africa.
Congo reports a deficit
of nearly 1,900 new Kingdom Halls.
Zambia reports a need
for over 900 new Kingdom Halls.
Mozambique and Angola each have a need
for almost 500 Kingdom Halls.
And in Nigeria they have on their books
a need for 2,000 renovations of Kingdom Halls
in addition to the new ones that they need.
And that’s not to mention all the work taking place
in major branch construction,
the construction of remote translation offices,
school facilities, Assembly Halls, and more.
Is there a need?
Absolutely!
Young ones, especially you young ones in your teens
thinking about how you will use your life,
can you get involved in the Bethel work
and theocratic construction work?
Should you?
If you do, what will your life be like?
Would you live to regret it?
Or is it possible that it would lead
to a most fulfilling life in this system of things?
Well, to help answer those questions, we invite you to watch the following video,
which highlights comments from ones who when they were young
made the decision to get involved in Bethel work
or in theocratic construction work.
Watching this video
could be like looking at your life in fast-forward.
If you choose the course that these ones chose,
how would that turn out for you?
Let’s watch.
My name is Pavel.
I serve at the Finland branch.
My name is Brad Bourquin.
I’m serving in the Congo.
My name is Gina Slay.
My name is Christopher Slay.
And we serve in the Nigeria branch.
My name is Karen Ferro.
I live in Argentina.
I grew up in a sign-language congregation because I have deaf parents.
And when I saw the Sign Language Department for the first time,
I was so impressed by it,
and so I developed my first love for Bethel service.

That seems unbelievable.
No nation does that.
But what is it that happens?
It is an act of God.
Jehovah puts that “one thought”
into the minds of the nations.
Yes, they will empower the United Nations
so that the United Nations will be in a position
to take action against false religion.
Now, this adjustment in understanding
also means that we have to adjust
our understanding of verses 12 and 13.
So if you’re in Revelation 17,
please, let’s look at verses 12 and 13:
“The ten horns that you saw mean ten kings
“who have not yet received a kingdom,
“but they do receive authority as kings
“for one hour with the wild beast.
“These have one thought,
so they give their power and authority to the wild beast.”
So up to now, we’ve assumed these “ten kings,”
which represent all the political powers and governments in the world at the moment,
did this during the last days by supporting,
first of all, the League of Nations and then the United Nations.
But now what do we understand this to be,
seeing we understand verse 17?
Well, there will come a time when all political powers on earth,
which includes many who have never been part
of the seven world powers,
will see that they need to collectively pool their power
by giving it to the United Nations
to try to solve some of the problems in the world.
And they will rule, notice, what does it say?
“For one hour”—just a short period of time.
So this newly empowered United Nations,
from that time on, will rule collectively for a short time,
but it will enable them to destroy false religion
and fight against Jesus and Jehovah’s people.
Now, isn’t that exciting?
But now we’re back to our subject again, you see, gradually things happen.
So we might say, ‘Well, yes, gradually, I see Babylon the Great
is losing influence in some places —maybe not yet—’
But don’t expect that you’ll see governments
gradually wanting to give over power.
They don’t want to do that.
It takes an act of God!
Jehovah will “put it into their hearts.”
This will occur with suddenness.
Yes, then the great tribulation will start
—a sudden change, not something that happens gradually.
So, what have we learned in our discussion?
Well, yes, some things change gradually.
But, brothers and sisters, remember there are some sudden things
that are about to occur.
Let’s remember the two things as a reminder.
First of all, the remaining anointed ones
will suddenly be taken to heaven while they are still very active.
The second one,
Jehovah will suddenly move the nations
to give their political power
to the United Nations.
So, what’s the takeaway?
Don’t be complacent.
Don’t think, ‘Oh, this is going to gradually change.’
No, some things won’t gradually change.
They will occur suddenly as acts of God!
So be ready, and don’t be surprised by sudden change!
Thank you, Brother Geoff.
You’ve given us much to think about.
We’ll probably have to watch that talk a few times to get all the points.
What a faith-strengthening program!
The second part of the annual meeting
will be featured as the broadcast for next month.
Now it’s time for our video postcard.
Let’s visit our brothers and sisters in Italy.
This is a land of rich history, vibrant culture,
and spectacular natural beauty
—from Lake Como and the Dolomites
in the north to the islands of Sicily
and Sardinia in the south.
Christianity found an early foothold
in Italy and spread rapidly.
Paul’s journeys took him to Syracuse;
Rhegium, known as Reggio today;
Rome; and Puteoli, near Naples.
The preaching work began
in modern-day Italy in 1891
when Brother C. T. Russell visited the small town of Pinerolo.
The first congregation of Jehovah’s Witnesses
was formed here in 1908.
Meetings were first held at the homes of two sisters.
Just as in the first century,
our brothers in the 20th century
faced stiff opposition.
The Fascist government and the clergy
suppressed the work of Jehovah’s Witnesses for decades,
but our brothers persevered.
For example, in 1925,
our brothers disguised their first assembly
as a wedding in this hotel.
And Brother Remigio Cuminetti
and Sister Albina Protti
were actually married during the assembly.
Today, the Italy branch supports
more than 250,000 publishers
in Italy and the tiny Republic of San Marino,
which is bordered by Italy on all sides.
Our brothers preach in ancient villages
like Alberobello,
known for limestone dwellings called trulli.
And they publicly witness in iconic cities,
such as Florence and Venice.
To assist congregations in Rome and Milan in the ministry,
a special initiative in 2023
encouraged neighboring congregations
to preach in those cities on the weekends.
Almost 13,000 publishers participated
and 63 new Bible studies were started!
Many refugees have come to Italy
from Africa, Asia,
and Eastern Europe.
To help our brothers learn to preach in a foreign language,
the Italy branch organized 420 courses
in 35 languages,
including Amharic, Sinhalese,
Twi, and Ukrainian.
Of course, our postcard from Italy would not be complete
without talking about food,
a delightful and important element
of Italian culture and tradition.
Along with its many wines, Italy is known for its regional cuisines,
including pizzas,
pastas, and cheeses,
such as Parmesan
and handmade mozzarella.
The brothers and sisters
from the Pinerolo Sud Congregation
send us their warm love and greetings.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

title: 제이컵 럼프: 예수의 이름으로 하는 기도에는 큰 힘이 있습니다 (요한 14:13, 14)

ko.text: “예수의 이름으로 기도드립니다. 아멘.”
우리는 항상 이 말을 합니다.
방금 전에 해설에서 들으신 것처럼 이 말은
여호와께 보내는 편지 끝에 서명을 하는 것과 같은
형식적인 절차가 아닙니다.
성구 해설에 나오는 것처럼 이 말은
예수가 대제사장이심을 인정하고
우리가 여호와께 나아가 기도할 수 있도록 길을 열어 준
대속 마련에 대해 감사하는 것입니다.
우리가 그처럼 감사를 나타내고 그와 일치하게 행동한다면
여호와께서는 우리의 기도를 들어주실 것입니다.
하지만 요한 14:13, 14의 성구를 생각해 보면
몇 가지 질문들이 생길 수 있습니다.
13절입니다. ‘여러분이 내 이름으로,
즉 예수의 이름으로 청하는 것은 무엇이든
내가 해 주겠습니다.’
14절도 비슷합니다.
“무엇이든지 여러분이 내 이름으로 청하면
내가 그것을 해 주겠습니다.”
이제 생각해 보시죠.
이 말씀은 예수께서 기도에 응답하신다는 뜻입니까?
예수께서 그 대화 중에 또 어떤 말씀을 하셨는지
요한 16:23을 보시겠습니다.
성경을 펴서 요한 16:23을 보시죠.
후반부만 읽어 보겠습니다.
23절. “진실로 진실로 여러분에게 말하는데,
여러분이 아버지께 무엇이든 청하면
그분이 내 이름으로 주실 것입니다.”
앞뒤가 좀 안 맞지 않나요?
예수께서는 “내 이름으로 청하면 내가 해 주겠다”고 하셨죠?
그런데 이 성구에서는 ‘내 이름으로 청하면
그분이, 다시 말해 여호와께서 주실 것’이라고 하셨습니다.
어떻게 된 것입니까?
이제 문맥을 조금 더 살펴보겠습니다.
26, 27절에 있는 예수의 말씀을 함께 보시겠습니다.
그분이 제자들에게 말씀하십니다.
“그날에는 여러분이 내 이름으로 아버지께 요청할 것입니다.
내가 여러분을 위해 요청하겠다는 말이 아닙니다.
아버지께서 친히 여러분에게 애정을 가지고 계십니다.”
따라서 우리가 기도할 때에 누가 우리를 도와주십니까?
「파수대」 2020년 4월호는 성구를 이렇게 설명합니다.
“우리의 기도를 듣고 응답해 주시는 분은
여호와이시지만
그분은 자신의 결정을 실행할 권한을
예수에게 주셨습니다.
여호와께서 듣고
기도에 어떻게 응답하실지 결정하시며
그분은 예수를 통해
우리에게 필요한 성령을 주심으로
기도에 응답하십니다.” 정말 놀랍죠?
그분은 의무감 때문이 아니라 사랑으로 그렇게 하십니다.
예수께서도 요한 16:27에서
아버지께서 여러분에게 애정을 가지고 계시다고 말씀하셨습니다.
연구 노트를 보면 이 단어는 다른 경우에도 사용되었습니다.
예수께서는 친구인 마리아와 마르다가
그들의 오라비이자 예수의 친구였던
나사로의 죽음을 슬퍼하는 것을 보셨을 때
그와 동일한 감정을 느끼셨습니다.
따라서 여호와와 예수께서는 사랑과 애정 때문에
우리의 기도에 응답하기 위해 노력하십니다.
따라서 기도에는 정말 대단한 힘이 있습니다.
여호와와 예수께서는 우리의 생각과 염려에 관심이 있으시며
기도에 응답하고 우리를 돕기 위해 노력하십니다.
한 명의 기도에도 이런 힘이 있습니다.
그렇다면 여러 명의 기도에는 얼마나 더 큰 힘이 있겠습니까?
이제 고린도 후서 1:11을 함께 보시겠습니다.
바울은 고린도 회중이 자신을 위해
어떤 기도를 할 수 있는지 말합니다. 11절.
“여러분도 간구의 기도로 우리를 도와줄 수 있습니다.
그렇게 한다면 많은 사람의 기도에 대한 응답으로
우리에게 베풀어지는 은혜를 두고
많은 사람이 우리 때문에 감사를 드리게 될 것입니다.”
한 번의 기도에도 힘이 있지만,
다른 한 사람이나 여러 사람을 위해
많은 사람이 함께 하는 기도에는 더 큰 힘이 있습니다.
이 구절에 대해 「통찰」 책에는 이런 설명이 있습니다.
“여호와 하느님이 인원수로 인해 압력을 느껴 행동하시는 분은 아니지만,
[자신의 종들이] 집단적으로 깊은 염려와 연합된 관심을 나타낼 때,
조처를 취하시는 분임은 분명하다.”
여호와께서 자신의 백성의 연합된 기도를 주의 깊이 들으시고
어떻게 예수를 통해 응답하시는지 성경의 예를 알아보겠습니다.
사도행전의 유명한 예인데요.
사도 12장을 직접 펴 보시기 바랍니다.
1절과 2절에서 당시 상황을 보시면
헤롯이 회중을 박해하면서 사도 야고보를
감옥에 가두었다가 처형해 죽입니다.
사도였던 사람이 처형된 거죠.
형제들과 다른 사도들의 심정이 어땠을지 생각해 보십시오.
이제 헤롯은 어떻게 합니까?
3절과 4절을 보면 베드로를 체포합니다.
그리고 감옥에 넣죠.
예전에 사도들이 감옥에서 도망한 적이 있기 때문에
두 군인이 베드로를 감시합니다.
「철」 책은 이렇게 설명합니다.
헤롯은 베드로를 “두 명의 보초병 사이에 쇠사슬로 묶어 놓고
16명의 보초병들이 24시간 내내 교대로 지키게 했습니다.”
헤롯은 베드로를 어떻게 할 생각이었습니까?
그를 죽일 생각이었습니다.
베드로가 그날 밤 얼마나 스트레스를 받았겠습니까?
‘내가 죽고 나면 내 아내는 누가 돌보지?
회중은 누가 돌봐야 할까?
예수의 양들은 어떡하지? 나한테 맡기셨는데’
하는 생각들을 했을지 모릅니다.
그는 아마도 이런 걱정을 하면서 간절히 기도했을 것입니다.
그러면 회중은 어떻게 베드로를 도왔습니까?
어떻게 했는지 5절을 보시죠. 5절.
“이렇게 베드로는 감옥에 갇혀 있었고,
회중은 그를 위해 [즉 베드로를 위해]
하느님께 [당연히 예수의 이름으로]
열렬히 기도를 드리고 있었다.”
여호와께서는 그 많은 기도에 대한 응답으로
어떻게 예수를 통해 베드로를 도와주셨습니까?
6, 7절입니다.
“헤롯이 그를 끌어내려던 참이었는데,
그 밤에 베드로는 두 개의 쇠사슬에 묶인 채
두 군인 사이에서 잠을 자고 있었고
문 앞에는 보초병들이 감옥을 지키고 있었다.
그때 갑자기 여호와의 천사가 나타나더니,
감방 안에 빛이 비쳤다.
천사는 베드로의 옆구리를 쳐서 깨우며
‘어서 일어나십시오!’ 하고 말했다.
그러자 쇠사슬이 그의 손에서 떨어져 나갔다.”
그러면 여호와께서는 어떻게 예수를 사용해 응답하셨습니까?
그분은 천사를 보내서 베드로를 풀어 주셨습니다.
하지만 이 성구의 세부점에 유의해 보십시오.
여호와께서는 베드로가 풀려나기 전에도
그의 필요를 돌봐 주셨습니다.
6절을 다시 보시면, 그는 자고 있었습니다.
깊이 잠들었죠.
여러분이 어린 시절에 깊이 자고 있는데
엄마가 와서 깨웠던 때를 기억하십니까?
엄마들은 불을 켜고 자녀들을 흔들면서 일어나라고 하죠.
자녀가 깊이 자고 있기 때문입니다.
천사도 바로 그렇게 했습니다.
베드로에게 빛을 비추었는데도 일어나지 않았습니다.
그래서 그의 옆구리를 부드럽게 쳤죠.
그런 다음 베드로에게 어서 일어나라고 말했습니다.
베드로는 잠에 너무 취해 있었기 때문에
그 후로도 한동안 상황을 제대로 파악하지 못한 것 같습니다.
무엇을 배울 수 있습니까?
그가 풀려날 때까지
“모든 이해를 뛰어넘는 하느님의 평화”를 받았다는 것입니다.

en.text: Well, “in Jesus name we pray, amen.”
We say that all the time,
and as Brother Montenegro just pointed out,
this is not just some technical thing,
like a signature at the end of a letter
that we send to Jehovah.
As we learned through the text today, our comments,
this is a recognition of Jesus’ role as High Priest
and appreciation for the ransom that make it possible to open the way,
or our approach, to Jehovah God.
So when Jehovah sees that gratitude
and when our actions back up that attitude,
well then, he’s going to listen to our prayers.
But we have maybe a few other questions
that we might have based on this scripture
at John 14:13, 14.
The Scripture says in verse 13:
“Whatever you ask in my name
[which we now understand, Jesus says] I will do this.”
And then you notice in verse 14, he says it again:
“If you ask anything in my name,
I will do it.”
So here’s the question:
Is Jesus answering our prayers?
Is that what he means?
Well, notice what Jesus says in the same conversation,
but just a little later
at John 16:23.
You can open your Bibles there to John 16:23.
We’ll just read the second half of that verse.
It says: “Most truly I say to you,
“if you ask the Father for anything,
he will give it to you in my name.”
Now, does this seem like a contradiction?
Didn’t Jesus say:
“If you ask anything in my name, I will do it”?
And now Jesus is saying:
‘If you ask anything in my name, He will give it to you.’
Jehovah will give it to you.
So, what’s the answer?
What’s going on?
Well, let’s balance this idea out just a little bit further.
In Jesus’ conversation in verses 26 and 27,
Jesus continues saying to his disciples:
“In that day you will make request
“of the Father in my name;
“in saying this, I do not mean that I will make request for you.
“For the Father himself
has affection for you.”
So who is it that’s working in our behalf when we pray?
Well, notice what The Watchtower  of April 2020 says
to explain this verse.
It says: “Although Jehovah is the one
“who hears and answers our prayers,
“he has given Jesus the authority
to carry out His decisions.”
So Jehovah listens.
He then decides on a plan,
a way of responding to the prayer,
and Jehovah follows through
by using Jesus to provide the holy spirit
that we need in answer to our prayer.
Amazing!
And neither of them are pressured to do this.
They do this because of love.
Jesus says this at the end of verse 27 —John 16:27:
“The Father himself has affection for you.”
So they don’t feel obligated.
The study note on that verse about the idea of affection says
that it’s the same deep emotion, or affection,
that Jesus showed
when he saw his friends Mary and Martha
grieving the death of Lazarus, their brother,
and who was also Jesus’ friend.
So Jehovah and Jesus, motivated by affection and love,
are working toward responding to our prayers.
So can you imagine the power that that means for us?
Jehovah and Jesus are interested in our thoughts,
interested in our concerns,
and are working toward answering and helping us.
So that’s with one prayer.
What happens when those prayers are multiplied in a large group?
Well, at 2 Corinthians 1:11,
Paul wrote this when he was talking about the prayers
that the congregation in Corinth would say for him.
He says: “You also can help us
“by your supplication for us,
“in order that many may give thanks in our behalf
“for the favor we receive
in answer to the prayers of many.”
So one prayer has power,
but a united prayer in behalf of someone
or a group of people has more power.
This is what the Insight  book says on this verse:
“While Jehovah God cannot be pressured by numbers into acting,
“he evidently takes . . . action
“when [his servants] collectively show
deep concern and united interest.”
So let’s see that in practice through a Bible example
of how Jehovah listens and responds
by using Jesus to the united prayers of his servants.
It’s a famous example in Acts chapter 12.
So open your Bibles, please, there to Acts chapter 12.
And we see in verses 1 and 2 the situation.
Herod is mistreating the congregation.
He puts James the apostle in prison,
and then he executes James —executes an apostle.
You can just imagine how this is affecting the brothers,
how this is affecting the other apostles.
And then what does he do next?
Well, in verses 3 and 4,
he then arrests Peter.
He puts him into prison.
He had Peter chained between two guards.
This is what the Bearing Thorough Witness  book says:
‘. . . chained between 2 guards at a time,
‘16 in total, working in shifts day and night
to make sure that this apostle didn’t escape,’
like the apostles escaped before in Acts chapter 5.
What was Herod wanting to do with Peter?
He wanted to execute Peter.
So can you imagine the stress that Peter would have had that night?
Remember, Peter was a married man.
‘Who’s going to take care of my wife?
‘Who’s going to take care of the congregation?
Who’s going to feed Jesus’ little sheep?’
Jesus told him, ‘This is what I want you to do.’
So all of these things were probably on his mind,
and he was praying about it.
But now, how could the congregation help Peter?
Well, they knew exactly what to do.
Verse 5 says:
“So Peter was being kept in the prison,
“but the congregation was intensely praying to God
[of course, in Jesus’ name] for him [for Peter].”
So how did this collective prayer move Jehovah
to use Jesus in following through and helping Peter?
Verses 6 and 7:
“When Herod was about to bring him out,
“that night Peter was sleeping
“bound with two chains between two soldiers,
“and guards in front of the door were keeping watch over the prison.
“But look!
“Jehovah’s angel was standing there,
“and a light shone in the prison cell.
“Hitting Peter on the side, he woke him,
“saying: ‘Get up quickly!’
And the chains fell off his hands.”
So how did Jehovah
respond in using Jesus?
Well, He sent an angel that was used to free Peter.
But do you notice the details of this verse?
Jehovah also understood Peter’s needs
until Peter’s situation would change.
It says here in verse 6 that he “was sleeping.”
How soundly?
Well, do you remember how soundly you were sleeping
when you were a little kid
and your mom would come in to wake you up?
She would turn on the light.
She might give you a little nudge on the side and tell you to get up.
Why?
Because you were sleeping soundly.
And that’s exactly what the angel did.
He shined the light on Peter.
Peter still didn’t wake up.
He then began hitting Peter,
of course, lovingly on his side
and had to tell him to get up quickly.
And it seems that Peter was so groggy that even later on,
he didn’t really quite understand what was going on.
So, what’s the point?
He received “the peace of God that surpasses all understanding”
until the situation changed.

title: 로널드 커잔: 여호와의 식탁에서 먹으십시오 (고린도 전서 10:21)

ko.text: “먹는 음식이 그 사람을 만든다.”
이 속담을 들어보셨을 겁니다.
우리는 어떤 음식을 먹을지 선택할 수 있습니다.
몸에 나쁜 음식도 있고 몸에 좋은 음식도 있습니다.
우리의 선택은 자신의 건강은 물론
여호와를 섬기는 데에도 영향을 줍니다.
우리가 먹는 음식이 그렇다면,
보는 것과 듣는 것도 우리를 만듭니다.
특히 오락의 선택은 큰 영향을 미칩니다.
우리는 살면서 매일 다양한 선택을 하게 됩니다.
우리는 “여호와의 식탁”에서 먹을 것입니까?
아니면 “악귀들의 식탁”에서 먹을 것입니까?
선택은 자유지만,
우리가 하는 선택에는 반드시 결과가 따릅니다.
여호와와 가까워질 수도 있고
멀어질 수도 있습니다.
오늘날 대부분의 사람들은 악귀들의 식탁에서 먹습니다.
우리는 그 결과를 분명히 볼 수 있죠.
그들의 행동을 보면, 그 식탁에 무엇이 차려져 있는지 알 수 있습니다.
그것은 바로 갈라디아서 5장에 나오는 “육체의 일”‏입니다.
그와는 달리,
우릴 포함해 전 세계 수백만 명의 증인들은
여호와의 식탁에서 먹기로 선택했습니다.
그리고 그 결과는 우리의 행동을 통해 분명히 드러나죠.
그분의 식탁에는 무엇이 있죠?
“영의 열매”‏가 차려져 있습니다.
분명한 사실이죠.
우리는 여호와의 식탁에서 먹는 걸 좋아합니다.
음식이 맛있고 영양가 있죠.
정말 분명한 사실입니다.
흥미롭게도 한 자매는 영적 양식에 대해 감사하는 편지를
중앙장로회에 보내 이렇게 말했습니다.
“언제나 변함없이 저희에게 맛있고 영양 많은 음식으로
영적 잔치를 마련해 주셔서 감사합니다.
계속 잔치 음식을 잘 먹기 때문에
영적으로 말해서 배가 점점 더 나오고 있습니다.
여호와의 양 떼를 먹이는 사명을 잘 수행해 주셔서 정말 감사합니다.”
모두가 동의하시죠?
영적 양식을 너무나 많이 먹기 때문에 배가 부르죠.
문자적인 의미가 아니라 영적인 의미에서 그렇습니다.
이 모든 양식에 대해 중앙장로회에 감사합니다.
요즘은 팬데믹 때문에
집에 있는 시간이 그 어느 때보다 많습니다.
혼자 있게 될 때도 많을 것입니다.
따라서 여호와와 가까워지는 데 도움이 되는 오락을 선택하기가 어려울 수 있습니다.
좋지 않은 오락을 선택하려는 유혹을 느낄 수도 있죠.
사탄은 우리가 혼자라는 것을,
때로는 외롭다는 것을 알고 있습니다.
그래서 마귀의 식탁에서 먹으라는 유혹에 넘어가기가
쉽다는 것을 알고 있습니다.
한 입 정도는 괜찮다고 유혹하죠.
「파수대」에는 이런 말이 있습니다.
“사탄은 …악한 것에 대한 사랑이 우리의 마음 한편을 차지하고 있다면
우리의 마음 다른 편에 옳은 것을 사랑하는 마음이 남아 있다 해도 상관하지 않습니다.”
그는 우리가 양쪽 식탁에서 먹으면
여호와에게서 멀어진다는 것을 압니다.
양쪽 식탁에서 먹는 게 가능합니까?
그렇게 하면 무슨 문제가 생깁니까?
오늘의 성구인 고린도 전서 10:21을
읽어 보시겠습니다.
10장 21절입니다.
“여러분이 여호와의 잔도 마시고
악귀들의 잔도 마실 수는 없습니다.
여러분이 ‘여호와의 식탁’에서도 먹고
악귀들의 식탁에서도 먹을 수는 없습니다.”
그러면 양쪽 식탁에서 먹는 게 가능합니까?
사실,
그렇습니다.
그래서 문제가 될 수 있죠.
그렇게 할 수는 있지만,
어떤 결과가 따릅니까?
일부 사람들은 남몰래 나쁜 것을 봅니다.
하지만 여호와는 어떻게 느끼십니까?
22절에 따르면
우리가 그런 식으로 행동할 때
여호와께서는 “질투”를 느끼십니다.
그분은 우리에게 전적인 정성을 원하십니다.
우리가 오직 그분의 식탁에서만 먹기를 바라시죠.
하지만 이렇게 정당화할 수도 있습니다.
‘내가 주로 여호와의 식탁에서 먹고,
가끔 한 번씩 악귀들의 식탁에서 조금씩 먹는 건 괜찮지 않나?
나는 진리 안에서 오래됐고
베델 봉사도 하고
출퇴근 봉사자나 원격 봉사자나 LDC 봉사자인데
난 장성해서 괜찮아.’
정말입니까?
12절을 보실까요?
“서 있다고 [다시 말해, 영적으로 강하다고] 생각하는 사람은
넘어지지 않도록 조심하십시오.
사람들이 일반적으로 받는 유혹 외에는
아무 유혹도 여러분에게 닥치지 않습니다.”
우리는 삶의 모든 면에서 전적인 정성을 나타내야 합니다.
예외란 없죠.
바울은 여호와께서 자신에게 헌신한 모든 사람에게
무엇을 요구하시는지 말한 것입니다.
31절을 보시죠.
“여러분은 먹든지 마시든지 [오락을 포함해] 그 밖에 무엇을 하든지,
모든 것을 하느님의 영광을 위해 하십시오.”
이게 우리의 목표죠.
사탄의 목표는 정반대입니다.
이 면에서 성경에는
우리에게 교훈을 주는 훌륭한 본들이 정말 많이 나옵니다.
예를 들어, 다윗왕은
언제나 여호와께 전적인 정성을 드리고
모든 일을 그분의 영광을 위해 하려고 했습니다.
이제 시편 101편을 펴 보시겠습니까?
101:1-8을 읽어 보겠습니다.
흥미롭게도
이 시를 읽어 보면 그가 여호와를 섬기면서 무슨 결심을 했는지,
다시 말해 어떤 일은 하고 어떤 일은 하지 않기로 했는지 알 수 있습니다.
그는 ‘~하겠다’라는 말을 여섯 번 함으로
어떤 사람을 자기 집에 들일 것인지,
누구와 교제할 것인지
분명히 결심했음을 나타냈습니다.
그럼 시편 101:1을 보시죠.
“내가 충성스러운 사랑과 공의를 노래하겠습니다.
오 여호와여, 당신에게 찬양 노래를 부르겠습니다.”
여호와를 찬양하고 그분을 섬기고 전적인 정성을 바치는 것이
다윗의 삶에서 가장 중요했습니다.
그 열망은 그가 하는 모든 선택과 그의 생각과
그의 말과 그의 행동에
영향을 미쳤습니다.
2절을 보시죠.
“내가 나무랄 데 없이 슬기롭게 행하겠습니다.”
그리고 이렇게 말합니다.
“당신은 언제 내게 오실 것입니까?”
그는 항상 그분과 가까이 있고 싶었습니다.
그는 말합니다.
“내가 집 안에서 마음의 충절로
걷겠습니다.”
따라서 다윗은 다른 사람과 함께 있을 때든
아무도 볼 수 없는 집 안에 혼자 있을 때든 한결같았습니다.
그는 여호와께 충절을 지키고
마음을 다한 사랑과 변함없는 정성을 다하겠다고 결심했습니다.
우리도 다윗이 한 것처럼
집 안에서나 베델 방에서도
충절로 걷겠다고 결심합니다.
아무도 우리를 볼 수 없어도
여호와는 보시니까요.
충절은 방화벽과 같습니다.
집 안이나 건물에 있는 방화벽은
불이 한 방에서 다른 방으로 번지지 않게 막아 주어
우리를 위험으로부터 보호해 줍니다.
또 다른 형태의 방화벽은
컴퓨터 보안 시스템에 사용됩니다.
해커나 바이러스가
네트워크나 컴퓨터에 침투하는 것을 막아 줍니다.
그와 비슷하게 우리도 자신만의 방화벽을 세워야 합니다.
성경으로 훈련받은 양심으로
나쁜 것은 차단하고
좋은 것만 받아들이는 겁니다.
부도덕이나 폭력이나 영매술처럼
우리에게 해로운 영향을 주는 것들을 완전히 차단하는 거죠.
여호와께서 미워하시니까요.
3절부터 8절의 내용을 보면
악귀들의 식탁에 차려진 오락물들의 메뉴 같다는 생각이 듭니다.
다윗이 지금 살아 있다고 상상해 보시죠.
그가 지금 손에 리모컨,
TV 리모컨을 들고 있습니다.
아니면 마우스로 인터넷을 하고 있습니다.
그러면 오늘날 우리가 보는 것들을 어떻게 느끼겠습니까?
3절을 읽어 보죠.
“무가치한 것[또는 쓸모없는 것]은
어느 것도 내 눈앞에 두지 않겠습니다.
내가 옳은 것에서 빗나가는 자들의 행위를 미워하니,
나는 그런 자들과 상대하지 않겠습니다.
구부러진 마음이 내게서 멀리 떨어져 있으니,
나는 악한 것을 받아들이지 않겠습니다.
이웃을 은밀히 중상하는 자는 내가 잠잠하게 하고.”
즉 채널을 돌리고 인터넷을 끄고 기기를 끄는 거죠.
“거만한 눈과 오만한 마음을 가진 자는 내가 용납하지 않겠습니다.
나는 땅의 충실한 자들을 눈여겨보아
내 곁에 살게 하겠습니다.
나무랄 데 없이 [또는 충절로] 걷는 자가
나를 섬길 것입니다.”
악한 것은 차단하고
좋은 것은 들어오게 하는 거죠.
“속이는 자는 내 집에 살지 못하고
거짓말쟁이도 내 앞에 [또는 내 눈앞에] 서지 못할 것입니다.
내가 아침마다 땅의 악한 자들을 모두 잠잠해지게 하리니,
즉 채널을 돌리고 인터넷을 끄고 기기를 끄는 거죠
행악자를 모두 여호와의 도시에서 끊어 버리려는 것입니다.”
다윗처럼 여호와를 섬기는 우리 모두는 매일 선택에 직면합니다.
무엇을 먹고
어디서 먹고
누구와 먹을 것인지 선택하죠.
선택에는 결과가 따릅니다.
신체적으로나 영적으로요.
여호와와 가까워질 수도 있고 멀어질 수도 있습니다.
최근 「파수대」는 우리에게 이렇게 자문해 볼 것을 권합니다.
“내가 선택하는 오락은
내가 위선적인 사람이라는 것을 드러내 주는가?
성서 연구생이나 관심자가 내가 선택하는 오락을 보면,
나를 말과 행동이 일치하는 사람이라고 여길 것인가?”
우리가 로마서 12:9의 교훈을 적용해
하느님에 대한 우리의 사랑에 언제나 “위선이 없게” 한다면
지혜로운 선택을 할 수 있을 것입니다.
기억하십시오.
음식이 그 사람을 만듭니다.
따라서 오직 여호와의 식탁에서만 계속 먹으시기 바랍니다.
그러면 그분께 전적인 정성을 드리고
‘모든 것을 그분의 영광을 위해’ 할 수 있습니다.

en.text: “You are what you eat.”
We all know that familiar saying.
It refers to things
that we may choose to eat.
Well, it could be junk food,
or it could be healthy food.
Our choices can impact us physically
as well as spiritually.
So if you are what you eat,
you are what you see and what you hear.
And that’s especially true when it comes to entertainment.
We’re reminded that each day we have a choice to make when we wake up.
Will we partake of “the table of Jehovah”
or “the table of demons”?
We’re free to choose,
but our choices have consequences.
They can draw us closer to Jehovah or could distance us.
Most today choose the table of the demons,
and the consequences are plain to see.
Their actions reflect what’s on the menu of the table of demons,
and that is “the works of the flesh,” listed in Galatians chapter 5.
In contrast, we who are tied in and millions around the world
have chosen to eat at the table of Jehovah.
And the actions and the consequences are evident as well.
What’s on Jehovah’s menu?
Well, it’s “the fruitage of the spirit.”
It’s very evident.
We love eating from Jehovah’s table.
It’s delicious, and it’s nutritious.
We all can attest to that.
It’s interesting that a sister sent a letter of appreciation
to the Governing Body about spiritual food.
This is what she said:
“Thank you for spoiling us with such a banquet of rich dishes
“that is constantly set before us.
“As we indulge in such feasting,
“we can say that our spiritual bellies are bulging
“because you have wholeheartedly fulfilled your commission
to feed Jehovah’s sheep.”
So I think we can all agree.
We have so much food that we’re getting; we are full.
We’re not talking about a physical belly; we’re talking about the spiritual belly here.
We appreciate the Governing Body blessing us with all this food.
Now, because of the pandemic,
of course, we’re at home now more than ever.
And perhaps we’re alone at times,
which brings up many challenges and temptations
about choosing the right kind of entertainment
that will draw us closer to Jehovah.
Now, Satan knows we’re alone.
He knows that sometimes we’re lonely,
so he may feel we’re more vulnerable,
or open, to temptation to partake of the table of demons.
Just a nibble, just a snack —will it really hurt?
You might remember this Watchtower  quote.
It says: “Satan does not mind if part of our heart is loving what is right
as long as part of it loves what is bad, what he promotes.”
He wants you to eat at both tables,
knowing that it could distance you from Jehovah.
So is it possible to eat at both tables?
What’s the harm?
Well, let’s read today’s Scriptural text
at 1 Corinthians 10:21.
As we recall, it says:
“You cannot be drinking the cup of Jehovah
“and the cup of demons;
“you cannot be partaking of ‘the table of Jehovah’
and the table of demons.”
So is it possible to eat at both tables?
Actually, yes.
But therein lies the problem.
You can do it.
But what are the consequences?
Some live a double life.
They try to eat at both tables.
How does Jehovah feel about that?
Notice verse 22.
It indicates that if we were to do so,
we would be “inciting Jehovah to jealousy.”
And we know he requires exclusive devotion.
He wants us to feed exclusively at his table.
However, we might rationalize:
‘If my main diet is at Jehovah’s table
‘and once in a while I nibble, or snack, at the table of demons, what’s the harm?
‘I’ve been in the truth for years.
‘I’ve been at Bethel for quite a few years’
or maybe: ‘I’m a commuter, a remote worker, LDC.
I can handle it. I’m mature.’
Really?
What does verse 12 say?
It says: “So let the one who thinks he is standing
“[so, spiritual]
“beware that he does not fall.
“No temptation has come upon you
except what is common to man.”
Exclusive devotion includes every aspect of our life
—no exceptions.
Paul reminds us of what Jehovah requires
of all those who have dedicated their lives to him.
Notice verse 31.
It says: “Whether you are eating or drinking
“or doing anything else [including entertainment],
do all things for God’s glory.”
That’s our goal.
But Satan’s goal is quite the opposite.
There are many Bible examples
that we can look to that really set a sterling example for us.
King David was one who always wanted to give Jehovah exclusive devotion,
to do all things for God’s glory.
In fact, open your Bibles to Psalm 101,
and we’re going to quickly read verses 1 through 8.
And it’s interesting that as we read his words,
we see the determination
in his service to Jehovah
—what he will do and what he refuses to do.
In fact, he says “I will” 11 times,
showing he was quite determined
in what he would allow into his house
or the associates that he would allow into his company.
Notice there at Psalm 101:1.
He says: “I will sing about your loyal love and justice.
To you, O Jehovah, I will sing praises.”
Yes, praising Jehovah, serving him, and giving him exclusive devotion
was the number one thing in David’s life.
It impacted all of his choices that he made
—what he thought about, what he said, what he did.
This led to actions.
Notice verse 2 says:
“I will act with discretion and blamelessness.”
And then he asked the question: “When will you come to me?”
He was always concerned about his closeness to Jehovah.
He said: “I will walk with integrity of heart inside my house.”
So it didn’t matter if David was with others
or if he was alone in his house where no one could see him.
He was determined to keep his integrity,
his wholehearted love,
and his unbreakable devotion to Jehovah.
Like David, we must be determined
to walk with integrity inside our house
—inside our Bethel room,
where others may not see us
but we know that Jehovah can.
Integrity is like a firewall.
A firewall is a wall within our home or an office building
that does not allow fire to spread from one room to the other.
It protects us from danger.
Well, another type of firewall is used on computer security systems
to prevent hackers and viruses
from infecting networks or computers.
Well, in the same way, we must build our own personal firewall,
that is, with our Bible-trained conscience
by not allowing bad things into our life
but only the good things from Jehovah
and making sure that these harmful influences
—like immorality, violence, and spiritism—
have nothing to do with us because we know Jehovah hates these.
As we read verses 3 through 8,
it’s almost like the menu
of what the entertainment is at the demons’ table.
And we can almost imagine that if David was alive today
and he had a remote control (TV remote control) in his hand
or a mouse and he was clicking through the Internet,
how he would view a lot of the things that we have access to today.
Notice verse 3.
He says: “I will not set anything worthless
“[or, “good-for-nothing,”] before my eyes.
“I hate the deeds of those who deviate from what is right;
“I will have nothing to do with them.
“A crooked heart is far from me.
“I will not accept what is bad.
Anyone slandering his neighbor in secret, I will silence.”
So change the station.
Exit the website.
Turn it off.
“Anyone with haughty eyes and an arrogant heart, I will not tolerate.
“I will look to the faithful ones of the earth,
“so that they may dwell with me.
The one walking in blamelessness [or, “in integrity”] will minister to me,”
so blocking out what is bad but allowing the good in.
Verse 7: “No deceitful person will dwell in my house,
“and no liar will stand in my presence [or, “in front of my eyes”].
“Every morning I will silence
“[change the station, exit the website, turn it off]
“all the wicked of the earth,
to cut off all wrongdoers from the city of Jehovah.”
So again, David as well as us and all loyal ones have a choice every day:
what we will eat, where we will eat,
whom we will eat with.
Our choices have consequences, both physically and spiritually.
They could draw us closer to Jehovah or they could distance us.
A recent Watchtower encouraged us to ask ourselves:
“Will my choice of entertainment
“make it seem that I’m hypocritical?
“If my Bible students or return visits saw the entertainment I choose,
would they think that I practice what I preach?”
We will make wise choices
if we apply the counsel at Romans 12:9
to always let our love for God “be without hypocrisy.”
So remember, you are what you eat.
So continue to eat and partake exclusively of Jehovah’s table
so that we can give him exclusive devotion
and “do all things for God’s glory.”

en.text: La la la la la la la la la.
I want to sing to Jehovah, just like Deborah did.
What inspired her to sing?
Come on!
Let’s have her tell us.
It’s a great story!
Hi, everyone. It’s me, Deborah!
During my time, the Israelites were very afraid.
Some even left their villages to hide.
Who were they afraid of?
This guy—Sisera.
He was chief of the Canaanite army.
They were all big bullies.
But was I afraid?
Not with Jehovah on my side.
Look, there I am!
I was a prophetess,
and Jehovah gave me good news
to tell Israel’s new leader, Barak.
I reassured him:
When you face Sisera, Jehovah will help you win.
I received courage from Jehovah,
and that gave Barak and the Israelites courage as well.
Jehovah defeated Sisera,
just like He promised.
And that’s why I was singing:
“Listen, you kings! . . . To Jehovah I will sing.”
Jehovah’s friends show courage.
Why not read the whole story
and let Deborah’s example encourage you?
Make time every day
to learn from Jehovah’s friends.
What do you think?
How did Deborah show
that she was Jehovah’s friend?
When is it hard for you to be courageous?
How can you help a friend be courageous?

title: M. 스티븐 레트: 고대 이스라엘은 전쟁을 했는데 오늘날 그리스도인들은 왜 전쟁을 하지 않습니까? (요한 1서 3:10-12)

ko.text: 이런 말이 있습니다.
전쟁은 사랑을 없앨 수 없지만
사랑은 전쟁을 없앨 수 있다.
여호와의 증인은 그 점을 보여 주는 좋은 예입니다.
그 어떤 끔찍한 전쟁도
여호와의 백성의 사랑을 없애지 못했습니다.
오히려 그 반대였죠.
그들의 사랑은 그들 가운데서 전쟁을 없애 버렸으며
마음속에서 증오심마저 없애 버렸습니다.
요한1서 3:10-12을 요약하면 이렇습니다.
‘하느님의 자녀와 마귀의 자녀는 이 사실로 분명히 드러납니다.
하느님의 자녀는 자기 형제를 사랑하지만
마귀의 자녀는 카인이 그랬던 것처럼 자기 형제를 죽입니다.’
그런데 이런 경험이 있으실까요?
봉사할 때나 다른 상황에서
그리스도인 중립에 대해 말하면서 전쟁에 참여하지 않는다고 하면
사람들은 흔히 이의를 제기하죠.
그리고 이스라엘 백성을 예로 듭니다.
“그들도 하느님의 백성이었는데 전쟁을 했잖아요.
그런데 왜 당신들은 전쟁을 안 하죠?”
그럴 때 뭐라고 하시겠습니까?
그런 사람들에게 설득력 있게 대답하려면
고대 이스라엘 백성과 오늘날 참그리스도인들 사이에
얼마나 큰 차이가 있는지 보여 주어야 할 것입니다.
적어도 다섯 가지 차이점이 있는데요.
첫 번째 차이점은 바로 이것입니다.
고대의 하느님의 백성은 하나의 나라였습니다.
따라서 그들이 이교 나라들과 전쟁을 할 때
동료 신자들이나 형제들을 죽이는 일은 없었습니다.
하지만 오늘날에는
계시록 7:9에서 알려 주듯이
큰 무리가 모든 나라와 민족과 종족과 언어에 흩어져 있습니다.
따라서 그리스도인들이 오늘날 전쟁에 참여하면 어떻게 될까요?
우리의 동료 신자들을 죽이게 될 것입니다.
하느님을 섬긴다고 주장하면서 전쟁에 참여하는 사람들이
실제로 그렇게 하고 있죠.
가톨릭교인들이 전쟁에서 가톨릭교인을 죽입니다.
다른 종교들도 마찬가지입니다.
기독교인이나 이슬람교인도
같은 종교를 믿는 사람들을 죽입니다.
여러 해 전에 한 교직자와 대화를 했는데요.
모르몬교의 고위 교직자였습니다.
전쟁에 대한 그들의 입장을 묻자 그가 말했죠.
“우린 전쟁을 싫어합니다.”
그래서 다시 물었습니다.
“만일 군대에 징집돼서 전쟁에 나가게 된다면 어떻게 하십니까?”
그 사람은 이렇게 말하더군요.
“국가는 그런 결정을 내릴 권리가 있으니까 나가서 싸워야죠.”
그래서 제가
다른 나라들에도 모르몬 신도들이 있는데
전쟁터에서 그들을 만나면 죽일 거냐고 물었습니다.
그는 모르몬교인이라면 살려 줄 거라고 했죠.
그래서 제가 말했습니다.
총을 쏘기 전에
종교를 일일이 물어볼 수는 없다고요.
그 사람이 인정은 하지 않았지만
분명히 요점은 파악했을 것입니다.
이제 두 번째 차이점입니다.
마음을 읽으시는 여호와 하느님께서는
이스라엘 백성의 적들이 심판받아 마땅하다고
직접 판결을 내리셨습니다.
그 적들은 자녀 희생과 심한 성적 부도덕을 통해
악귀를 섬기는 사람들이었습니다.
그래서 그분은 이스라엘에게
자신의 심판을 집행하라고 직접 명령하셨습니다.
이제 레위기 18장을 펴서
여호와께서 가나안 민족과 관련해
이스라엘 백성에게 어떤 명령을 내리시는지 직접 보시죠.
그분의 말씀입니다.
읽어 드리죠.
“이 중에서 어떤 것으로도
너희 자신을 부정하게 만들어서는 안 된다.
내가 너희 앞에서 쫓아내는 민족들이
바로 이 모든 것으로 자신을 부정하게 만들었다.
그래서 그 땅도 부정하다.
나는 그 잘못 때문에 그 땅을 처벌할 것이며,
그 땅은 주민들을 토해 낼 것이다.”
이처럼 여호와께서 심판 집행을 명령하신 거죠.
세 번째는 적들을 무차별적으로 죽이지 않았다는 겁니다.
많은 예들이 있지만 그중 두 가지만 살펴보겠습니다.
여호수아 6장을 보면
라합은 물론 그의 가족 모두가
기적으로 목숨을 건집니다.
라합이 여호와께 믿음을 나타냈기 때문이죠.
또 여호수아 9장과 10장을 보면
여호와께서 원래 멸망시키기로 되어 있던 기브온 사람들을
살려 주신 내용이 나옵니다.
그들이 여호와께 믿음을 나타냈기 때문이죠.
이스라엘 시대와 비교해 볼 때 오늘날 전쟁은 어떻죠?
순종하고 믿음을 나타내면 목숨을 건질 수 있습니까?
아니죠.
전쟁에서 폭탄이 터지면
보통 군인들보다 민간인들이 더 많이 사망합니다.
일단 전쟁이 벌어지면
수많은 무고한 사람들이 죽임을 당합니다.
네 번째 차이점은
이스라엘 군인들이 여호와께서 주신 지침에 따라
전쟁을 수행해야 했다는 것입니다.
여호와께서 주신 그러한 지침들 중 몇 가지만 살펴보겠습니다.
신명기 23장을 펴 보실까요?
신명기 23장.
여호와께서 이스라엘 군인들에게 어떤 명령을 하셨는지 보시죠.
신명기 23장 9절입니다.
“당신은 적들을 대적하여 진을 칠 때
온갖 나쁜 일을 피해야 합니다.”
12절입니다.
“당신은 진영 밖에 한 장소를 정해 두어야 합니다.”
네, 그곳에 가서 용변을 보아야 했습니다.
그 이유를 14절에서 보시죠.
“당신의 하느님 여호와께서
당신을 구출하고 적들을 당신에게 넘겨주려고
당신의 진영 안을 다니시므로 진영은 거룩해야 합니다.
그래야 그분이 당신에게서 불결한 것을 보시고
당신과 함께하지 않고 떠나시는 일이 없을 것입니다.”
이스라엘 군대가 여호와의 거룩한 전쟁을 하고 있었기 때문에
여호와께서는 이스라엘 군인들에게 깨끗함을 요구하셨습니다.
오늘날 전쟁에 참여하는 군인들은 어떠한가요?
정말 다르지 않나요?
「통찰」 책을 보면
이스라엘 군인들은 정복한 도시들의 여자들을
결코 성폭행해서는 안 되었고,
한 달 동안은 그 여자들과 결혼할 수도 없었습니다.
「통찰」 책 “군대” 제하에서
여호와께서 이스라엘 군인들에게 주신 지침을 더 많이 볼 수 있습니다.
마지막 차이점은
여호와께서 이스라엘과 함께 싸우셔서
기적적인 승리를 주셨다는 것입니다.
이번에도 많은 예들 중에서 두 가지만 생각해 보죠.
예리코에서 어떤 일이 있었습니까?
제사장들이 나팔을 불고
군대가 행진을 하고
군인들이 함성을 지르자
성벽이 무너져 내렸습니다.
여호와께서 승리를 주신 거죠.
또 다른 예로,
기브온 사람들은 가나안 왕들이 연합해서 공격했을 때
어떻게 승리를 거두었습니까?
여호수아 10:11을 보면
‘여호와께서 하늘에서 큰 우박을 쏟아부으셔서
우박 때문에 죽은 자가
칼에 죽은 자보다 많았습니다.’
분명 여호와께서 이스라엘과 함께 싸우신 겁니다.
이렇게 다섯 가지입니다.
첫째, 오늘날과는 달리 고대 하느님의 백성은
한 나라를 이루고 있었습니다.
따라서 전쟁에서 형제를 죽이는 일은 없었죠.
둘째로, 하느님은 자신이 직접 심판한 자들을 멸망시키셨습니다.
셋째로, 이스라엘 군인들은 적들을 무차별적으로 죽이지 않았습니다.
넷째, 이스라엘 군인들은
여호와께서 주신 엄격한 지침에 따라 전쟁을 했습니다.
다섯째, 하느님은 이스라엘과 함께 싸우셔서
기적으로 그들에게 승리를 주셨습니다.
정리하자면 이스라엘이 한 전쟁은 거룩한 전쟁이었죠.
하지만 오늘날 이 세상의 전쟁들은
전혀 거룩하지 않습니다.
예수께서도 그리스도인들이 하는 전쟁에서는
실제 무기를 사용하지 않을 거라고 하셨습니다.
그분은 마태 26:52에서 “칼을 잡는 사람은 모두
칼로 망할 것”이라고 말씀하셨습니다.
또한 제자들에게 적들을 해치지 말고
그들을 위해 기도하라고 가르치셨죠.
이러한 예수의 말씀은
이사야서에 나오는 여호와의 예언과도 일치합니다.
이사야 2:2-4에 따르면
“말일에”
하느님의 백성은 “칼을 쳐서 보습을 만들고”
전쟁에 참여하기는 커녕 ‘다시는 전쟁을 배우지도 않을 것입니다.’

en.text: Now, there is a saying
that war can’t kill love,
but love can kill war.
And Jehovah’s Witnesses
truly exemplify that saying.
All of man’s horrible wars
have not killed off the love of Jehovah’s people,
and, in fact, it has made us stronger.
And yet, their love
has killed off war among their ranks
and even from within their hearts.
First John 3:10-12 in essence says:
‘The children of God and the children of the Devil
‘are evident by this fact:
‘The children of God love their brothers.
‘The children of the Devil slaughter their brothers
like Cain slaughtered his brother.’
But, you know, sometimes in the ministry and in other places
when we try to bring up our stand regarding not participating in war
—our Christian neutrality—
people bring up the objection about the Israelites.
They’ll say: “Well, they were God’s people. They fought wars.
So why can’t Christians fight in wars?”
How do you deal with that argument?
Well, if you’re going to overcome that,
you obviously have to show them that there’s a vast difference
between the Israelites in Bible times
and true Christians today.
In fact, let’s briefly discuss five differences.
Number one, in the days of the Israelites,
God’s people were gathered into one nation.
So when they went into battle against the pagan nations,
they weren’t killing fellow believers.
They weren’t killing their brothers.
But today Revelation 7:9 says
that the ‘great crowd of true Christians
‘is scattered in all nations,
tribes, peoples, and tongues.’
So if Christians participated in war today, what would happen?
We would end up killing fellow believers —our brothers.
And, of course, we know that is happening
among ones who claim to be God’s people
“who take up the sword.”
We find Catholics killing their fellow Catholics.
We find the same thing among the Methodists,
the Baptists, Muslims
—slaughtering members of their own religion.
It makes me think of a conversation I had many years ago
with a high-ranking Mormon elder.
And I asked him, I said, “Well, what is your position on war?”
He said, “We don’t like war.”
I said, “But what do you do, though, if you’re living in a country
at a time when there’s a draft and you’re drafted into the military?”
He said, “Well, if the government makes us do it,
“it’s their responsibility.
We go ahead and fight.”
I said: “Do you then kill another Mormon on the battlefield?
Because I know you have Mormons in many different countries.”
He said, “Well, if I knew he was a Mormon, I’d let him go.”
I said, “But normally it’s not possible
to check with each person before you shoot them.”
Well, he didn’t admit it,
but obviously he got the point that was made there.
But now, let’s go to our second difference.
Jehovah God, who can read hearts,
personally judged as worthy of execution
the people that the Israelites went up against.
He directly told them
to execute his judgment on these demon-worshipping people
whose worship included gross sexual immorality
—even child sacrifice.
Open up to Leviticus chapter 18, please,
and notice an example of Jehovah
telling the Israelites this concerning the Canaanites.
Now, here’s what he said.
At Leviticus 18:24,
Jehovah says:
“Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these things,
“for it is by all these things that the nations
“that I am driving out from before you
“have made themselves unclean.
“Therefore, the land is unclean,
“and I will bring punishment on it for its error,
and the land will vomit its inhabitants out.”
So Jehovah told them to execute his judgment on these people.
Now, here’s our third difference:
The Israelite wars killed selectively,
and we have just two examples of many that could be related.
Joshua chapter 6
shows that Rahab and her entire household
were miraculously spared.
Why?
Because Rahab exercised faith in Jehovah.
Or what about Joshua chapters 9 and 10?
It talks about how Jehovah
spared the Gibeonites
who were actually in line for destruction
because they exercised faith in Jehovah.
Now, those are just a couple of examples.
But in today’s wars,
are people spared because of their obedience and faith?
No.
Often the civilian casualties are greater than the soldier casualties
when they drop their bombs.
The collateral damage, as they call it,
often results in the substantial death
of innocent people.
Let’s get our fourth difference now.
The Israelite soldiers
were required to conduct their warfare
according to Jehovah’s guidelines.
Now, here are just a few examples of Jehovah’s guidelines
of many that could be related.
Open up to Deuteronomy chapter 23, please,
Deuteronomy 23,
and notice what Jehovah told the Israelite army,
the soldiers.
Deuteronomy 23, beginning in verse 9:
“When you are encamped against your enemies,
you should avoid anything bad.”
Look at verse 12:
“A private place should be designated for use outside the camp.”
They would go out there and relieve themselves.
Why?
Look at verse 14:
“For Jehovah your God
“is walking about within your camp to deliver you
“and to hand over your enemies to you,
“and your camp must be holy,
“so that he does not see anything indecent in you
and turn away from accompanying you.”
Yes, Jehovah required cleanliness
among these Israelite soldiers
because actually they were sanctified for warfare.
But now, what about soldiers today?
It’s obviously very different.
In fact, the Insight  book talks
about how they were certainly not allowed to rape
any of the conquered cities’ women.
In fact, they couldn’t even marry such a woman for one month.
On page 173 of the Insight  book,
you can get a lot of Jehovah’s guidelines
that he gave to the Israelite soldiers.
Now, one more difference:
Jehovah fought with the Israelites,
giving them miraculous victories.
And again, we’ll just give two examples of many that could be related.
How was the battle of Jericho won?
Well, the priests blew horns,
the military force marched,
the army shouted,
and the walls fell flat.
Jehovah gave them that victory.
Or what about the victory
of the Gibeonites,
the victory over the kings that attacked them?
Joshua 10:11 says:
“Jehovah hurled great hailstones
“from the sky . . .
“[so that] more died from the hail
than from the sword of the Israelites.”
Well, unlike today, Jehovah fought with the Israelites.
So there we have five differences.
First, in the days of the Israelites
—see, unlike today God’s people were gathered in one nation.
So they didn’t go up against their brothers when they went into war.
And second, Jehovah personally judged those executed as worthy of such.
Third, the Israelite wars
were killing only selectively.
And fourth, the Israelite soldiers were required to conduct their warfare
according to Jehovah’s strict guidelines.
And fifth, Jehovah fought with the Israelites,
giving them miraculous victories.
So you could truly say that the Israelite wars were holy wars.
But the wars of today’s wicked world are anything but holy.
No wonder Jesus said that theocratic warfare
would no longer include the use of physical weapons!
Remember what he said in Matthew 26:52?
He said: “Those who take up the sword
will [die, or] perish by the sword.”
And he taught his followers not to harm their enemies
—in fact, to even pray for them.
And his position, of course, is in harmony with Jehovah’s prophecy
at Isaiah 2:2-4,
that “in the final part of the days,”
God’s people would “beat their swords into plowshares”
and they would not even “learn war anymore”
—much less participate in it.

title: 데이비드 셰이퍼: 영적 양식을 섭취함으로 “깨어 살피십시오” (마태 24:42-45)

ko.text: 예수 그리스도께서는 마지막 때에 일어날 일들에 관해 이야기하시면서
오늘의 성구에 나오는 이러한 경고의 말씀을 하셨습니다.
문맥과 함께 읽어 보시죠.
마태복음 24:42-45입니다.
“그러므로 깨어 살피십시오.
여러분의 주가 어느 날에 올지 여러분이 모르기 때문입니다.
그러나 한 가지는 알아 두십시오.
도둑이 밤 몇 시에 올지 집주인이 알았더라면, 깨어 있으면서
집에 도둑이 침입하지 못하게 했을 것입니다.
그러므로 여러분도 준비하고 있으십시오.
여러분[즉 제자들]이 생각지도 않은 시간에
‘사람의 아들’이 올 것이기 때문입니다.
주인이 자기 집안 일꾼들을 돌보도록 임명하여
그들에게 제때에 양식을 나누어 주게 한 충실하고 슬기로운 종은 과연 누구입니까?”
유의하셨습니까?
“깨어 살피라”고 했죠.
여기서 “깨어 살피라”는 말은
예수께서 여호와의 심판을 집행하러 오실 때 우리 모두가 준비를 갖추고 있고,
옳은 일을 하고 있고, 그분이 제자들에게 맡기신 일을 부지런히 하고 있어야 한다는 말이죠.
어떻게 그렇게 할 수 있을까요?
45절을 다시 보시면 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 나오죠.
이 종은 집안 일꾼들에게
“제때에 양식을” 나누어줍니다.
그리고 일꾼들은 이 양식을 통해 준비를 갖추게 되죠.
그러면 근래에 들어 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”을 통해 밝혀진
몇 가지 중요한 점들에 관해 생각해 보겠습니다.
예를 들어 연구용 「파수대」 2000년 5월 15일호
14면 27항에서는 이러한 내용을 볼 수 있습니다.
‘몇 가지 세부 점만 빼고 다니엘서에 나오는 예언들이 모두 성취되었다.’
어떤 세부점일까요?
그 기사의 28항에서는 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
“다니엘 11장을 연구해 보면, ‘북방 왕’과 ‘남방 왕’ 사이의 세력 다툼도
최종 단계에 접어들었다는 것을 알게 됩니다.”
이 내용이 깨어 살피는 데 도움이 됐죠.
또 「파수대」 2012년 6월 15일호 기사
“여호와께서 ‘반드시 곧 일어날’ 일을 밝혀 주십니다”에서는
다니엘의 예언에 관해 더 많은 점을 알려 줍니다.
느부갓네살이 꿈에서 본 형상과 일부는 강하고 일부는 약한 발가락 부분에 관해 설명했죠.
그리고 “남방 왕”에 관해 이렇게 말했습니다.
“일반 사람들은 철 같은 힘을 발휘할 영미 세계 강국의 능력을 약화시키고 있습니다.
또한 정치인들 간의 상반된 이념과 근소한 차이밖에 나지 않는 선거 결과 때문에,
인기 있는 지도자들조차 권력의 기반이 약해져서
자신의 공약을 이행할 확실한 권한을 가질 수 없게 되었습니다.”
이 기사는 2012년에 발행되었는데 우리가 깨어 살피는 데 도움이 됐죠.
좀 더 최근에 2020년 5월호 연구용 「파수대」에도 다니엘 11장에 관해 다루는 3개의 기사가 실렸죠.
그 기사들에 실린 새로 조정된 내용들을 기억하시나요?
그중 두 가지만 살펴보시죠.
먼저 다니엘 11:41에는 “북방 왕”이 아름다운 땅으로 들어간다는 내용이 나옵니다.
과거에는 냉전 시대에 당시 “북방 왕” 소련이
참그리스도인들을 박해하고 활동을 제한함으로 아름다운 땅에 들어갔다고 이해했습니다.
하지만 2020년 5월호에서는 “북방 왕”이 그때뿐 아니라 마지막 날 기간 내내
여러 차례 아름다운 땅에 들어갔다고 설명했습니다.
예를 들어 출판물과 전파 활동과 집회를 금지하고,
조직의 자산을 몰수하고, 하느님의 백성을 박해하고 죽이기까지 했죠.
이 명확해진 이해도 우리가 깨어 살피고 박해를 받아도 낙담하지 않는 데 도움이 됩니다.
두 번째로 5월호 연구용 「파수대」에서는 다니엘 11:44, 45에 관해서도 다루는데
거기서는 “북방 왕”이 “동쪽과 북쪽에서 나오는 소문 때문에 당황할 것”이라고 예언합니다.
그 기사는 이 예언을 “큰 우박”이 하느님의 적들에게 비처럼 쏟아질 것이라고 한
요한 계시록 16:21의 예언과 연관 짓습니다.
이 우박이 무엇인지는 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 이미 밝혀 주었죠.
그 상징적인 우박은 여호와의 백성이 전하는 강력한 심판의 소식을 가리킬 수 있습니다.
그리고 그 기사 15면에는 이런 내용도 나옵니다.
마곡의 곡 즉 나라들의 연합체는 아마도
그 우박 같은 소식에 자극을 받아 하느님의 백성을 공격하려고 할 것입니다.
네. 이러한 영적 양식은 우리에게 큰 도움이 됩니다.
우리가 준비를 갖추고, 옳은 일을 하고,
예수께서 마지막 때에 제자들에게 맡기신 일을 부지런히 하게 해 주죠.
우리는 집회와 출판물을 통해
현재 세상 상태와 성경에서 예언하는 끝이 오기 직전의 상황을 비교하는 법을 배웁니다.
그래서 세상에서 벌어지는 일들과 사람들의 태도, 정치적 상황,
하느님의 백성의 영적 상태와 활동이
성경에서 예언하는 끝이 오기 직전의 상황과 정확히 일치한다는 것을 알게 됩니다.
하지만 어떤 사람은 이렇게 질문할지 모릅니다.
‘마태복음 24:3에 나오는 “세상 제도의 종결”이
좀 더 미래의, 세상 상태가 지금보다 훨씬 더 나빠질 미래의 어느 때를 가리키는 것은 아닙니까?’
「파수대」 2015년 8월 15일호에서는 그 흥미로운 질문을 다루고 있습니다.
답이 무엇이었죠?
또 다른 질문들로 그 답을 알려 줍니다.
‘“큰 환난” 전에 세상 상태가 얼마나 나빠질 것이라고 생각합니까?
예를 들어, 어느 나라에서나 전쟁이 벌어지고,
식탁에 오를 식품이 하나도 없고, 집집마다 환자가 있을 것이라고 생각합니까?
그런 상황이라면,
회의적인 사람들도 성경 예언이 성취되고 있다는 것을 인정하지 않을 수 없을 것입니다.
하지만 예수께서는 대부분의 사람들이 “유의하지 않고” 일상생활에 몰두하다가
끝이 왔음을 뒤늦게 깨닫게 될 것이라고 하셨습니다.’
따라서 표징은 누구나 준비를 갖춰야겠다고 생각할 만큼 너무 분명해서는 안 됩니다.
표징을 보고 인정하는 사람도 있고 유의하지 않는 사람도 있어야 할 것입니다.
이 점을 아는 것도 깨어 살피는 데 도움이 됩니다.
하지만 이렇게 생각하시는 분이 계실지 모릅니다.
‘난 이미 오래 기다렸는데 우박 같은 소식을 전하는 일은 언제 시작되는 거야?
나는 살아서 끝을 못 볼 것 같은데.’
그러면, 우리가 깨어 있을 필요가 없나요?
“충실하고 슬기로운 종”은 이 점에 관해 무엇이라고 알려 줍니까?
배부용 「파수대」 2020년 제2호 15면에는 이런 격려적인 내용이 들어 있습니다.
“1세기에 살았던 예수의 제자들은 … 고통과 고난이 모두 사라지는 것을 보지는 못했습니다.
하지만 그런 어려움으로부터 보호를 받았습니다.
어떻게 말입니까?
그들은 하느님의 의로운 표준에 따라 살면서,
그 표준을 무시하는 사람들이 겪은 어려움으로부터 보호를 받았습니다.
[또] 왕국이 올 것이라는 확고한 믿음은 그들이 극심한 시련을 겪을 때 도움이 되었습니다.
또한 하느님께서는 그들이 어려움에 대처[하고 놀라운 일들을 이룰] 수 있도록
‘정상적인 것을 초월하는 능력’을 주셨습니다.”
네, 그들은 충절을 지키며 인내했기 때문에 지금 큰 축복을 누리고 있습니다.
그리고 그 축복은 지금부터 영원히 지속될 것입니다.
그들의 믿음을 본받는 사람도 모두 축복을 받을 것입니다.
인내할 힘이 나지 않습니까?
우리는 예수께서 언제 심판하러 오실지 모릅니다.
하지만 여호와께서 주시는 영양가 높은 영적 양식을 잘 섭취한다면 준비를 갖출 수 있을 것입니다.

en.text: When discussing events that would occur
in the time of the end,
Jesus Christ gave the warning
that’s recorded in our day’s text.
Let’s read it in its context, please
—Matthew chapter 24,
verses 42-45.
It says: “Know one thing [that’s verse 43].”
It says: “Keep on the watch, therefore,
“because you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
“But know one thing:
“If the householder had known in what watch the thief was coming,
“he would have kept awake and not allowed his house to be broken into.
“On this account, you too prove yourselves ready,
“because . . . at an hour that you [you disciples]
do not think to be it [the Son of man is coming]”
—“at an hour that you do not think to be it.”
And then it says:
“Who really is the faithful and discreet slave
“whom his master appointed over his domestics,
to give them their food at the proper time?”
Well, what does it mean for us to “keep on the watch”?
As Jesus indicated, it means that when he comes
as Jehovah’s executional agent,
we want to be ready,
we want to be acting appropriately,
and we want to be busy in the work
that he has assigned his true followers to do.
And how do we do that?
Notice that verse 45 draws our attention
to “the faithful and discreet slave,”
a slave that would give the domestics
“their food at the proper time,”
food that would enable them to be ready.
For instance, consider some of the things
that we have been learning
with the help of “the faithful and discreet slave” recently.
The Watchtower  of May 15, 2000,
page 14, paragraph 27, had this to say:
“All the prophecies in the book of Daniel
“have been fulfilled
except for a few details.”
And what are those details?
Paragraph 28 continued that “a study of Daniel chapter 11
“shows that the conflict
“between ‘the king of the north’ and ‘the king of the south’
has reached its final stages.”
Well, that helped us keep on the watch.
Further light on Daniel’s prophecy came
in The Watchtower  of June 15, 2012,
in the article “Jehovah Reveals What ‘Must Shortly Take Place.’”
There, in explaining the significance of Nebuchadnezzar’s dream image
and the toes that prove partly strong and partly fragile,
The Watchtower  said this regarding “the king of the south”:
“The common people undermine
“the ability of the Anglo-American World Power
“to act with ironlike strength.
“Also, opposing ideologies and close election results
“that do not end up in a clear majority
“have weakened the power base of even popular leaders,
“so that they have no clear mandate
to implement their policies.”
That was in 2012.
Well, that helped us to keep on the watch.
And lately we received
the May 2020 study edition of The Watchtower
containing three study articles that center on Daniel chapter 11.
Do you recall some of the new points from that issue?
There were many, but here are two.
First, we used to feel that “the king of the north,”
or the Soviet Union at the time,
entered into what Daniel 11:41 calls “the land of the Decoration”
during the Cold War
by persecuting genuine Christians
and limiting, although not stopping, their activity.
But now, the May study edition has expanded that application,
saying that “the king of the north” entered into “the land of the Decoration”
on a number of occasions throughout the last days.
It has done so by banning our publications,
our preaching work, and our meetings
and by confiscating our property
and by persecuting and killing God’s people.
This clear understanding is helping people keep on the watch
and not become discouraged by persecution.
A second point in that May study edition is this:
Daniel 11:44, 45 says
that “the king of the north,” regarding “the king of the north,”
he’s concerned about “reports out of the east and out of the north.”
They disturb him.
And that third study article links that prophecy
to Revelation 16:21,
which foretells “great hailstones” that rain down on God’s enemies.
Well, “the faithful and discreet slave” has already said that this symbolic hailstorm
may take the form of a hard-hitting judgment message
delivered by Jehovah’s people.
But this study article on page 15
even goes so far as to say
that it could be that this message,
this hailstone message itself,
is what provokes Gog of Magog, or the coalition of nations,
into attacking God’s people.
Well, this kind of spiritual feeding helps us to be ready,
helps us to act appropriately,
helps us to be busy in the work
that Jesus has assigned for his true disciples
in this time at the end.
Well, at our meetings and through our publications,
we are trained to compare the world situation
with what the Bible says would be happening right before the end.
And what do we find?
That the events, the attitudes, the political circumstances,
and the condition and activity of God’s people
match exactly what the Bible says
would be in evidence right before the end.
Still, some might ask,
‘Couldn’t that term Jesus used in Matthew 24:3,
‘“conclusion of the system of things,”
‘refer to a yet future time
when world conditions will be even worse?’
Again, The Watchtower posed that very question
in the August 15, 2015, issue.
How did it answer that question?
With yet another question, namely,
“How bad do you expect conditions to become before ‘the great tribulation’?
“For example, [it continued]
“do you expect that there will be a war in every country,
“no food on anyone’s table, and illness in every household?
“Under those conditions, even skeptics would likely feel compelled
“to admit that Bible prophecy was undergoing fulfillment.
“However, Jesus said that most people would take ‘no note’ of his presence,
carrying on with life’s normal activities until it is too late”
—a reference to Matthew 24:37-39.
So the fulfillment of the sign can’t be so obvious
that we are forced to be ready.
There has to be space for people
either to acknowledge the sign or take no note.
Well, that thought also helps us to keep on the watch.
“But I’ve been waiting a long time,
“and I haven’t yet participated in the hailstone work.
“What if I don’t personally live to see
the end of this system of things?”
Again, what do we learn
from “the faithful and discreet slave”?
Did you notice this beautiful point
in the 2020 Watchtower,
public edition, number two, page 15.
It said: “Even though Jesus’ disciples in the first century . . .
“did not see the end of all pain and suffering in their lifetime . . . ,
“they were protected.
“How?
“They lived by God’s righteous standards,
“and that protected them from the difficulties suffered
“by those who ignored what God said.
“Their strong faith that the Kingdom would come
“helped them to face even the severest of problems.
“And God gave them ‘the power beyond what is normal,’
so that they could cope” with challenges
and achieve remarkable goals.
And we could add that because of their record

title: 하느님을 섬기려면 꼭 종교 단체에 소속되어야 합니까?

ko.text: 많은 사람은 하느님을 믿으며, 하느님과 가까워지고 싶어 합니다.
하지만 종교 단체에 소속되기보다는
혼자서 믿음 생활을 하려고 하죠.
이유가 무엇입니까?
일부 사람은 종교 단체가 저지른 폭력 행위와
종교 지도자들의 위선적인 행동에 크게 실망했습니다.
또 종교가 이 시대에는 도움이 되지 않는다고 생각하는 사람도 있죠.
하느님을 섬기려면 꼭 종교 단체에 소속되어야 합니까?
하느님은 어떻게 생각하실까요?
성경은 과거에 충실한 사람들이 하느님을 어떻게 섬겼는지 알려 줍니다.
예를 들어 하느님의 친구라고 불릴 만큼 그분과 친밀했던 아브라함은
여러 사람과 함께 하느님을 섬겼습니다.
그는 하느님의 표준에 따라 살았고,
가족과 종들도 그렇게 하도록 가르쳤습니다.
다른 많은 충실한 가장들도
여러 사람과 함께 하느님을 섬겼습니다.
나중에 하느님께서는 고대 이스라엘 사람들과 1세기 그리스도인들에게
함께 모여 숭배하라고 명령하셨습니다.
그들은 함께 성경을 읽고
성구 설명을 듣고
노래를 부르고
기도를 했습니다.
이처럼 하느님을 숭배하기 위해 함께 모인 사람들의 집단을
회중이라고 불렀습니다.
성경에서는 1세기 소아시아와 유럽 전역에 여러 회중이 있었다고 알려 줍니다.
또 우리가 혼자서 하느님을 숭배해도 된다면
성경의 일부 조언들은 앞뒤가 맞지 않는 말이 될 것입니다.
예를 들어 고린도 전서 1:10에서는
하느님을 섬기는 사람들 사이에서
분열이 없게 하고, 일치되게 말하고, 연합되어야 한다고 조언합니다.
그런데 혼자서 하느님 섬긴다면 어떻게 이 조언을 따를 수 있겠습니까?
따라서 분명 하느님은
우리가 하느님을 섬기는 회중에 소속되어
그분을 찬양하고 숭배하기를 바라십니다.
하느님의 회중에 있는 사람들은 서로를 진심으로 아끼고 사랑합니다.
그리고 당신처럼 하느님에 대해 더 배우고 싶어 하죠.
그러면 하느님이 승인하시는 종교 단체를 어떻게 찾을 수 있을까요?
이러한 점과 그 밖의 문제들에 대한 성경의 가르침을 알아보려면
jw.org를 방문해 보세요.

en.text: Many people today believe in God
and are interested in spirituality.
Yet, instead of turning to organized religion,
they choose to practice spirituality on their own.
Why?
Some have been disillusioned by religiously based violence
and the hypocrisy of religious leaders
or have dismissed religion as irrelevant.
Must you belong to an organized religion to worship God?
What’s God’s view?
The Bible tells us how faithful people in the past worshipped God,
people such as Abraham.
Abraham had a personal relationship with his Creator.
‘He even came to be called God’s friend.’
He lived by God’s standards
and taught his household to do the same.
Like many other faithful people in the Bible,
Abraham worshipped as part of a community
with family and servants.
Later, God required the ancient Israelites
and first-century Christians to worship together as a group.
Those gatherings included
reading and explaining scriptures,
singing, and praying together.
God’s worshippers were organized into what were called congregations.
The Bible mentions congregations
found throughout first-century Asia Minor and Europe.
In fact, many statements in the Bible would make little sense
if God did not require us to worship him as part of a congregation.
For example, 1 Corinthians 1:10 says
that his worshippers should not be divided.
Rather, they should be united and in agreement on spiritual matters.
How could someone apply this direction
if his or her worship was independent and detached from others?
The Biblical evidence clearly shows
that God wants you to serve him and offer him praise
as a part of his congregation of people.
He wants you to meet and worship alongside people
who truly care about one another
and who, like you, are interested in learning more about him.
But you may wonder, ‘If there is an organized religion
God approves of, how can I find it today?’
To learn more about what the Bible says on this and many other topics,
go to jw.org.
