ko.text: 여호와께서는 자신의 종들이 예수에 대한 사랑을 나타내려고 매일 노력하는 것을 기뻐하시죠.
예수께서도 그 점을 요한 14:23에서 이렇게 분명히 밝히셨습니다.
“누구든지 나를 사랑하면 내 말을 지킬 것입니다.
그러면 내 아버지께서 그를 사랑하실 것입니다.”
여러분이 최선을 다해 이 말씀을 따르는 모습은 정말 격려적입니다.
여러분은 왕국에 대해 전파하기 위해 힘과 시간을 바쳐 열심히 일하고 있습니다.
그에 더해 예수와 여호와의 충성스러운 친구들인 여러분은
헌금을 함으로 왕국을 꾸준히 지원하고 있습니다.
형편이 닿는 데까지 관대하게 기부하고 있죠.
여호와께서는 예수께서 하시는 일에 대해
우리가 그처럼 감사를 표현하는 것을 매우 소중히 여기십니다.
중앙장로회는 여러분의 사랑에 대해 깊은 감사를 표현해 줄 것을 제게 요청했습니다.
잊지 마시기 바랍니다.
여러분의 기부에는 정말 큰 힘이 있습니다.
2020년 6월부터 발행된 “우리의 헌금은 어디에 사용됩니까?” 연재 기사는 그 점을 잘 보여 줍니다.
각각의 기사는 우리의 헌금이 왕국 활동에 어떻게 사용되고 있는지 잘 알려 줍니다.
그럼 여러분의 기부가 그 후에도 영향을 미쳤을까요?
여러분의 헌금이 어떻게 계속 힘을 발휘하고 있는지 이어지는 영상을 보시겠습니다.
에콰도르에 있는 한 원주민 공동체가 우리 형제들의 숭배의 자유를 침해하자,
헌법 재판소에서 이 중요한 문제에 대한 재판이 열렸습니다.
원주민 공동체도 국제 수준에 맞춰 인권을 존중해야 하는가 하는 문제였죠.
재판소는 우리에게 승소 판결을 내렸습니다.
형제들의 관대한 기부와 여호와의 축복 덕분에 좋은 판결이 나올 수 있었습니다.
이제 이 판결은 하나의 좋은 판례가 되어
세계 전역에서 진행되는 다른 비슷한 사건들에서도 잘 활용되고 있습니다.
그 판결은 전 세계의 형제 자매들이 거둔 큰 승리였습니다.
하지만 우리를 반대했던 그 원주민 거주 지역에서도 긍정적인 변화가 있었습니다.
그 지역 사람들은 소수의 현지 형제들이 속해 있는 조직의 큰 규모에 깜짝 놀랐습니다.
그들은 여호와의 증인에 대해 더 알게 되면서 우리를 더 존중하게 되었습니다.
이제 형제들은 반대를 받는 것이 아니라 지역 주민들과 평화롭게 지내고 있습니다.
예를 들어, 한 회중은 전도인이 53명인데 2024년 기념식에 106명이 참석했습니다.
전도인이 크게 늘면서,
아프리카에서는 다른 모든 대륙을 합친 것만큼 많은 왕국회관 공사가 필요해졌습니다.
하지만 공사 비용이 여전히 큰 문제입니다.
예를 들어, 탄자니아에선 약 2500만 명이 하루에 고작 2달러 정도 되는 돈으로 살아가죠.
하지만 왕국회관을 신축하려면 무려 5만 달러가 듭니다.
현지 전도인들과 전 세계 형제들의 헌금 덕분에
세계 어디서나 왕국회관을 신축하거나 개축할 수 있게 되어 전도인들이 많은 유익을 얻고 있습니다.
저희 마핑가 회중은 왕국회관 개축으로 많은 유익을 얻었습니다.
아주 품위 있는 숭배 장소가 되었죠.
동영상도 잘 볼 수 있게 되었습니다.
지역 사회에서도 좋은 증거가 되었고 집회 참석자가 많이 늘었습니다.
전 세계의 형제들을 통해 이렇게 도와주신 여호와께 감사합니다.
성경을 번역하는 데는 여러 해가 걸립니다.
번역자들이 그 긴 시간 동안 일해야 하죠.
우리 조직은 형제들의 헌금을 사용해 번역에 도움이 되는 프로그램들을 마련해 주었습니다.
그 덕분에 성경을 더 분명하고 이해하기 쉽게 번역할 수 있죠.
외딴 지역에서는 성경을 구하기가 아주 어렵습니다.
한 가지 예로 통브 지역의 한 회중은 성경 한 권을 모든 전도인이 돌려 보았는데,
그 성경은 이해하기도 어려웠습니다.
2018년에 「신세계역 성경」이 킬루바어로 발행되자
단지 1년 만에 전도인이 20퍼센트 넘게 증가했습니다.
분명 킬루바어로 발행된 성경은 형제 자매들에게 엄청난 영향을 미치고 있습니다.
여러분의 헌금에 얼마나 큰 힘이 있는지 보면서 믿음이 더 강해지셨죠?
혹시 헌금을 더 하고 싶지만 경제적으로 여유가 없으십니까?
만일 그렇다면, 기부에 관한 이러한 성구를 기억하시기 바랍니다.
“그분은 우리가 가지지 않은 것이 아니라 가진 것에 따라 주기를 바라십니다.”
가진 것에 따라 관대하게 기부한다면 예수에 대한 사랑을 나타낼 수 있습니다.
기억하십시오.
여러분의 헌금은 의미 있고 소중하며 큰 힘이 있습니다.
그리스도에 대한 여러분의 사랑이
형제들에게 발휘하는 힘을 계속 보게 되시기를 기도합니다.
여러분의 모든 지원에 진심으로 감사합니다.

en.text: Jehovah appreciates the effort made
by his worshippers each day
to show their love for his Son, Jesus.
In his statement recorded at John 14:23,
Jesus himself made this point clear:
“If anyone loves me,
“he will observe my word,
and my Father will love him.”
It is truly beautiful to observe how you have embraced his word.
You are tirelessly devoting time and physical power
to advance the work of preaching about the Kingdom.
As loyal friends of Jesus and Jehovah,
you have also shown steadfast support for the Kingdom
through your monetary donations.
Within your means,
you have given generously.
Jehovah highly esteems these powerful gifts,
which are expressions of love for what his Son is doing.
The brothers of the Governing Body have asked me
to express their deep appreciation for the love you have shown.
We want to reassure you
that your donations have a powerful impact.
Since June 2020,
the article series “How Your Donations Are Used”
has chronicled this power.
Each one tells a story highlighting
how donations are being used to further the Kingdom work.
Have you ever wondered
what happened after the article was published?
In the following video, notice how your donations
continue to have a powerful effect.
After an indigenous community
opposed the freedom of worship of our brothers in Ecuador,
the constitutional court heard a court case
regarding this fundamental issue:
Should the indigenous communities
respect international human rights?
The court accepted our reasoning and decided yes!
With the loving support through the donations from our brotherhood
and Jehovah’s blessing on this issue,
the court ruling is available
and has already been used for legal argument
in other similar cases and in other parts of the world.
This court decision was a great victory
for our brothers and sisters around the world.
But if we think about the community where the opposition arose,
we can see the encouraging progress.
The community was surprised by the size of the organization
behind this small group of local publishers.
The more the community got to know Jehovah’s Witnesses,
the more they respected and valued us.
Now instead of experiencing opposition,
our brothers enjoy a peaceful relationship with the community.
For example, the congregation of 53 publishers
enjoyed a Memorial attendance of 106 in 2024.
Because of the tremendous growth,
Africa has about the same need
for new Kingdom Halls and major renovations
as all the other continents combined.
The cost of construction in Africa continues to be a challenge.
In Tanzania, for example,
where about 25 million Tanzanians live on less than $2 (U.S.) a day,
building a new Kingdom Hall can cost over $50,000 (U.S.).
Thanks to the donations of local publishers,
along with those from the global brotherhood,
publishers are able to enjoy new and renovated Kingdom Halls
in all parts of the world.
Here in Mafinga,
we benefited from a renovation
of our Kingdom Hall.
It is a place of worship that is respectable.
Now we even get the videos easily.
Truly, it has given a very good witness in the community
and has attracted many to the meetings.
We thank Jehovah for this provision of support
through our worldwide brotherhood.
Translating the Bible takes many years.
Therefore, it requires thousands of hours
of work by the translators.
Through the donations made by the brothers and sisters,
we use a translation tool developed by the organization.
This tool helps us to translate the Bible in a clear and understandable way.
In certain remote areas,
access to the Bible is a big challenge.
In Tombe, for example,
a congregation had only one Bible to share among all the publishers,
and that translation of the Bible was difficult to understand.
After the release of the Kiluba New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures
we had an increase of more than 20 percent of publishers
in just one year.
It is clear that the Word of God in Kiluba
has had a big impact on our brothers and sisters.
We are confident that seeing the impact of your donations
strengthens your faith.
But what if you have little materially?
Perhaps you wish you could give more.
If that is how you feel,
remember what the Bible says about our gifts to Jehovah:
“It is especially acceptable according to what a person has,
not according to what a person does not have.”
Your generosity with what you have
is what shows how much you love the Christ.
And rest assured,
your donations are meaningful, appreciated,
and they have power.
It is our prayer that you will continue to see the power
that your love of the Christ has on your brothers.
Thank you for all you have done and will continue to do.

ko.text: JW 방송에 오신 여러분을 환영합니다.
이번 달로 JW 방송이 시작된 지 10년이 되었습니다.
이 방송이 하느님의 백성을 연합시키는 데 어떤 특별한 역할을 했는지 볼 것입니다.
“성경 원칙 적용하기”에 포함되는 이 동영상의 1부를 기억하시나요?
제임스와 린다는 끝이 언제 올지에 지나치게 신경을 썼었죠.
이 부부가 다른 사람이 미래에 대해 균형 잡힌 견해를 갖도록 어떻게 도와주는지 볼 것입니다.
「철이 철을 날카롭게 한다」에서는
우리의 웹사이트를 봉사에서 활용하는 방법을 알아볼 것입니다.
이제 2024년 10월 JW 방송을 시작하겠습니다.
제가 처음 베델 봉사를 시작했을 때 가족과 통화하려고 집에 전화를 걸면
어머닌 늘 이렇게 말씀하셨죠.
“아마겟돈 언제 시작되는지 들었니?”
물론 농담으로 하신 말씀이었지만
그 질문에서 느낄 수 있듯이 우리 모두는 여호와께서 약속하신 신세계를 간절히 기다립니다.
혹시 여호와께 “얼마나 더 기다려야 하나요?” 하고 말씀드려 본 적 있으신가요?
또는 이렇게 말씀드렸을지도 모르죠.
“지쳐서 더는 못 버틸 것 같아요.
이 세상의 문제들에서 벗어나 영원한 평화를 누리게 해 주실 것이라는 약속은
대체 언제 이뤄지는 건가요?”
누구나 이런 생각을 하게 될 수 있죠.
그러면 영적인 전쟁에서 지쳐 포기하지 않는 데 무엇이 도움이 됩니까?
마가 13:29에 나오는 예수의 말씀을 읽어 보시죠.
“이와 같이 여러분도 이런 일들이 일어나는 것을 보거든 그가 문 앞에 가까이 있다는 것을 아십시오.”
여기 언급된 이런 일들이란 무엇일까요?
예언이 성취되는 것을 가리키죠.
성경 예언들이 성취되는 것을 보게 되면 우리의 믿음이 강해집니다.
끝이 가깝고 신세계가 눈앞에 있다는 것을 느끼게 되죠.
그러면 인내할 힘을 얻게 됩니다.
어떤 예언들이 있을까요?
지진, ‘전쟁, 전쟁에 관한 소문’, 식량 부족, 역병에 관한 예언들이 동시에 이루어지고 있습니다.
우린 “이런 일들이 일어나는 것을 보고” 있죠.
또한 하느님에 대한 사랑이 식고 사람들의 태도가 전반적으로 나빠지고 있습니다.
디모데 후서 3장에 예언된 대로이죠.
디모데 후서 3:13은 이렇게 말합니다.
‘악한 사람들과 속이는 사람들은 더욱더 악해질 것입니다.’
우린 “이런 일들이 일어나는 것을 보고” 있죠.
예언대로 “왕국의 좋은 소식”이 전 세계에서 전파되고 있습니다.
1000개가 넘는 언어로 말이죠.
우린 “이런 일들이 일어나는 것을 보고” 있습니다.
그리스도의 통치 덕분에 여호와에 대한 지식이 풍부하게 되었습니다.
우린 “이런 일들이 일어나는 것을 보고” 있죠.
이사야 45:18은 어떤가요?
그 성구에서는 여호와를 땅을 ‘만드신 분’으로 언급하면서
그분이 “땅을 헛되이 창조하지 않으시고 사람이 거주하도록 지으셨다”고 말합니다.
과학자들은 이대로 가다가는 지구에 사람이 살 수 없게 될 것이라고 말합니다.
지구 온난화를 해결하기 위해 즉각 조처를 취하지 않으면
돌이킬 수 없는 결과를 겪게 될 것이라고 경고하고 있죠.
계시록 11:18에서는 오늘날 사람들이 “땅을 파멸”시킬 것이라고 예언했죠.
이 예언 역시 여호와께서 땅이 완전히 파멸되지 않도록 개입하실 것이라는 점을 보증해 줍니다.
어떤 사람들은 세상 상태가 얼마나 더 악화될지 궁금해할 수 있습니다.
흥미롭게도 예수께서는 누가 17:20에서 이렇게 말씀하셨죠.
“하느님의 왕국은 뚜렷이 볼 수 있게 오는 것이 아닙니다.”
이 성구는 마지막 날에 사람들이 끝이 가깝다는 것을 인정할 수밖에 없을 정도로
세상 상태가 극단적으로 나빠지지는 않을 것임을 알려 줍니다.
마태 24:37-39에서 알려 주듯이 사람들은 “먹고 마시고” 결혼하고 일상생활을 할 것입니다.
이 점을 생각할 때 우린 어떻게 해야 할까요?
포기하지 않겠다고 결심해야 하죠.
마가 13:35에서 예수께서는 “깨어 살피십시오”라고 말씀하셨습니다.
깨어서 경계를 늦추지 말라고 하신 거죠.
평행 기록인 마태 24장을 보면
예수께서는 깨어 있는 것을 준비하고 있는 것과 연관 지으셨습니다.
우리가 지칠 때에도 그런 태도를 갖는 데 무엇이 도움이 될까요?
계속 앞으로 나아갈 힘을 어디에서 얻을 수 있습니까?
바로 신뢰심을 갖는 것입니다.
우리 모두는 여호와를 사랑하죠.
우리는 우리 각자에 대한 여호와의 충성스러운 사랑을 확신해야 합니다.
우리는 그분이 늘 우리를 도와주실 것임을 신뢰할 수 있습니까?
히브리서 13:5에서 여호와께서 뭐라고 보증하시는지 함께 보시죠.
“내가 결코 너를 떠나지 않겠고 결코 너를 버리지 않겠다.”
여호와께서는 지금까지 우리를 붙들어 주셨습니다.
어떤 경험이 떠오르시나요?
어쩌면 여러분은 자연재해 때문에 큰 피해를 입었을지 모릅니다.
하지만 그분이 붙들어 주셨죠.
사랑하는 사람과 사별했을 때도 그분이 붙들어 주셨을 겁니다.
어떤 시련을 겪을 때이든 우리는 여호와께서 도와주시는 것을 경험했죠.
따라서 그분은 앞으로도 우리를 붙들어 주실 것입니다.
우리가 가진 확신이 시편 46:1, 2에 이렇게 표현되어 있습니다.
“하느님은 우리의 도피처와 힘, 고난의 때에 쉽게 찾을 수 있는 도움이시다.
그러므로 우리는 두려워하지 않으리,
땅이 변해도, 산들이 바다 깊은 곳으로 무너져 내려도.”
이 성구에 나오는 표현은 여호와께서 우리를 돌봐 주실 것이라는 점을 분명히 알려 줍니다.
이 점을 기억하는 것이 왜 중요할까요?
히브리서 13:6에서는 그러한 확신과 용기를 연관 짓고 있습니다.
그 성구를 함께 읽어 볼까요?
“그러므로 우리는 확신에 차서 이렇게 말합니다.
‘여호와가 나를 돕는 분이시니 내가 두려워하지 않겠다.
사람이 내게 무엇을 할 수 있겠는가?’”
이 성구에서는 우리를 돕는 분이나 그들을 돕는 분이 아니라 “나를 돕는 분”이라고 했죠.
우린 여호와를 사랑합니다.
그리고 여호와께서도 우리를 사랑하시며
우리 각자를 도와주실 것임을 절대적으로 확신할 수 있죠.
때로는 여호와께서 우리 각자를 사랑하시고
우리를 도우실 것이라는 점을 신뢰하기 어려울 수 있습니다.
여호와의 사랑에 대한 신뢰심을 어떻게 기를 수 있을까요?
3가지 방법을 살펴보죠.
첫 번째 방법을 잠언 15장에서 찾아볼까요?
9절을 읽어 보겠습니다.
“여호와께서는 악한 자의 길은 혐오하시지만, 의를 추구하는 자는 사랑하신다.”
이 성구에 보니까 ‘여호와께서 의를 추구하는 자는 사랑하신다’고 했죠.
그분은 우리가 완벽하게 의로울 수 없다는 것을 아십니다.
하지만 우리가 최선을 다하기 때문에 사랑해 주시죠.
“의를 추구하는” 일을 중단하지 않기 때문에 사랑하시는 겁니다.
우리가 포기하지 않고 의를 추구한다면 그분은 결코 우리를 버리지 않으실 것입니다.
둘째로, 자신의 마음을 여호와께 쏟아 놓으십시오.
예레미야 애가 2:19에는 이런 말이 나옵니다.
“네 마음을 여호와의 면전에 물처럼 쏟아 놓아라.”
이 성구에서는 우리의 생각이 아니라 우리의 마음을 쏟아 놓으라고 했습니다.
우리의 감정, 걱정, 염려를 쏟아 놓으라고 한 것이죠.
물을 남김없이 쏟아 놓는 것처럼 우리의 마음을 쏟아 놓으라고 한 것이죠.
우리는 하늘에 계신 아버지께 사랑과 감사를 표현하고,
우리의 걱정거리와 우리가 원하는 것을 말씀드리고,
그분의 인도를 구함으로 하느님과의 우정을 소중히 여긴다는 것을 나타낼 수 있습니다.
그렇게 하면 어떤 결과가 있을까요?
자신의 마음을 물처럼 쏟아 놓고 그분의 응답을 개인적으로 경험할수록
그분의 사랑을 더 깊이 느끼게 되고
그분이 결코 버리지 않으실 것이라는 확신이 강해질 것입니다.
여호와의 변함없는 사랑에 대해 감사하는 마음이 더 커지겠죠.
셋째로, 시련을 겪는다고 해서 여호와의 승인을 잃은 것은 아니라는 점을 기억해야 합니다.
우리의 적은 우리가 여호와를 가깝게 느낄 때 힘을 얻는다는 것을 알고 있습니다.
그래서 우리의 확신을 약화시키려고 하고 우리가 여호와에게서 멀어지기를 바라죠.
예를 들어 욥이 큰 시련을 겪을 때 그를 위로하러 온 사람들은
그가 하느님의 승인을 잃었기 때문에 그런 시련을 겪는 것이라고 진실이 아닌 말을 했습니다.
여호와께서는 욥이 창조물에 주의를 기울이고 그분의 사랑과 지혜를 깨닫도록 도와주셨습니다.
충실한 욥은 어떤 반응을 보였을까요?
욥기 42:5에서 이렇게 말했죠.
“제가 주에 대해 귀로만 들었으나 이제 눈으로 주를 분명히 봅니다.”
우리도 여호와의 승인을 잃었다는 생각이 들 수 있습니다.
그럴 때 여호와께 그분을 보고
매일 그분의 충성스러운 사랑을 느낄 수 있게 해 달라고 청해야 합니다.
현재 겪는 시련을 통해
그분에 대한 사랑과 신뢰심을 더 키울 수 있게 도와 달라고 요청하십시오.
이렇게 해서 앞으로 일어날 일에 어떻게 대비할 수 있는지 생각해 봤는데요.
바로 여호와의 충성스러운 사랑에 대한 신뢰심을 키우는 것입니다.
여호와께서 결코 버리지 않으실 것임을 신뢰하면
계속 영적 싸움을 싸우고 깨어 살피게 될 것입니다.
에베소 6:16에서는 여호와에 대한 믿음 즉 신뢰심을 방패에 비합니다.
그 방패로 “악한 자의 불화살을 모두 끌 수 있다”고 했습니다.

중앙장로회는 성경 원칙들을 가르쳐 주었고 계속 힘을 내게 도와주었습니다.

그로 인해 여러 어려움을 겪고 있다는 걸 깨달았습니다.
그 형제 이야기에 공감이 되었어요.

가족이 같이 앉아서 왕국 노래 연습도 하고, 성경 이야기도 읽고,

여호와의 증인의 대회에 처음 갔는데, 온 사람이 만 명은 되는 것 같았어요.
근데 거기 모인 사람들은 생긴 것도 피부색도 다 달랐어요.
여호와께서 말씀하시는 것 같았죠.
“라피카, 기억하니?

봐, 난 차별하지 않아.

절 돌봐 주시는 하늘의 아버지께서 계시다는 걸 아는 것만큼 기쁜 일이 또 있을까요?

말레이시아에는 다양한 민족이 살고 있어서 옷, 언어, 음식도 아주 다양합니다.
1930년대에 선교인들이 이 나라에 왔고 진리가 전해지기 시작했습니다.
1950년대 초에 첫 번째 회중이 생겼죠.
일부 선교인들은 한 달에 15건의 연구를 사회했습니다.
형제들은 진실한 마음을 가진 사람들을 계속 찾고 있습니다.
5000명이 넘는 전도인들이 각자 약 한 건의 성서 연구를 사회하고 있습니다!
물가에는 기둥들 위에 지어진 작은 집들이 모여 하나의 긴 집을 이루고 있는데,
그곳에서 많은 성서 연구가 사회됩니다.
잠언 9:3에서는 ‘지혜가 여종들을 보내, 높은 곳들에서 외치게 한다’고 말합니다.
말레이시아의 자매들은 실제로 그렇게 하고 있죠.
높은 키나발루산을 오르고 숲의 다리를 건너며 봉사합니다.
케닝가우 회중에 있는 89명의 전도인들이 여러분 모두에게 사랑과 인사를 전합니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting®.
This month marks ten years since the first program debuted.
We’ll take a look at the special role
JW Broadcasting has played in uniting God’s people.
In Part 1 of the episode of Applying Bible Principles,
James and Linda were too focused on when the end would come.
We’ll see how they now help others keep a balanced view of the future.
In Iron Sharpens Iron,
we’ll learn how to put our website to better use in the ministry.
This is the October 2024 edition
of JW Broadcasting.
When I first began serving at Bethel,
I’d call home to speak with my family
and my mother would always ask,
“Have they told you when the date
of Armageddon is?”
Though she was being humorous and didn’t expect an answer,
her question reveals what we all long for
—Jehovah’s promised new world.
Maybe you have, in a sense, asked Jehovah that question,
“How much longer, Jehovah?”
Or you’ve said to Jehovah: “I’m exhausted.
“I don’t know how much longer I can keep going.
“Please, Jehovah, when will your promises for a world of lasting peace,
refreshment, and relief from the pressures of this world come true?”
We all likely feel this way from time to time.
What can help us not give up,
not give out, in our spiritual battle?
Note the words of Jesus at Mark 13:29.
Notice what he says: “Likewise also you,
“when you see these things happening,
know that he is near at the doors.”
What things would we see happening?
Prophecy being fulfilled.
When we recognize Bible prophecies being fulfilled before our eyes,
our faith is fortified.
We see that the end is imminent.
We recognize that we’re almost done.
That helps us not give out.
What are some of these prophecies?
You’re familiar with the prophecies of earthquakes,
“wars and reports of wars,” food shortages,
and disease all happening at once.
“You see these things happening.”
We see the diminished love of God
and the deteriorating attitude of people in general,
as foretold in 2 Timothy chapter 3.
Second Timothy 3:13 says:
“Wicked men and impostors
will advance from bad to worse.”
“You see these things happening.”
As foretold, “this good news of the Kingdom” is being preached worldwide
—now in over 1,000 languages.
“You see these things happening.”
As a result of Christ’s rule,
the knowledge of Jehovah is abundantly overflowing.
“You see these things happening.”
And what about Isaiah 45:18?
Here Jehovah calls himself the “Maker” of the earth,
“who did not create it simply for nothing,
but formed it to be inhabited.”
Today, scientists say that the world is on the brink of becoming uninhabitable.
They warn that if action to stop global warming is not taken quickly,
its compounding effects will become irreversible.
At Revelation 11:18,
the Bible foretold that in our day,
man would be “ruining the earth,”
and it also assures us
that Jehovah will step in and not let the earth be completely ruined.
Some may wonder how much worse things will get.
Interestingly, at Luke 17:20,
Jesus said this
“The Kingdom of God is not coming with striking observableness.”
This means that world conditions during the last days
would not be so extreme
that people would be forced to believe that the end is near.
As Matthew 24:37-39 indicates,
they would still be “eating and drinking,”
getting married, and able to carry on their everyday lives.
How should this affect us?
It should fortify us not to give up.
At Mark 13:35,
Jesus said we must “keep on the watch.”
This means to stay awake and be on guard.
And in the parallel account in Matthew 24,
Jesus connects this with being ready.
What will help us to do this when we feel so exhausted?
Where can we get strength to keep up the fight?
In a word—trust.
We all love Jehovah.
We want to be convinced
of Jehovah’s loyal love for us individually.
Can we trust that he’ll always be there to help us?
Notice on-screen the assurance Jehovah gives
at Hebrews 13:5:
“I will never leave you,
and I will never abandon you.”
Jehovah has been sustaining us.
Think how he sustains you.
Maybe you’ve experienced the ravages of a natural disaster;
Jehovah has sustained you.
Maybe you’ve dealt with the loss of a loved one;
Jehovah has sustained you.
Whatever trial we’ve gone through,
we can see how Jehovah has helped us.
This confirms for us that he’ll sustain us in the future.
And we have the confidence
that’s stated at Psalm 46:1, 2:
“God is our refuge and strength,
“a help that is readily found in times of distress.
“That is why we will not fear, though the earth undergoes change,
though the mountains topple into the depths of the sea.”
These emphatic expressions leave no doubt
that Jehovah will care for us.
Why is this reminder so important?
Well, verse 6 of Hebrews chapter 13
links trust with courage.
Notice what it says:
“So that we may be of good courage and say:
‘‘‘Jehovah is my helper; I will not be afraid.
What can man do to me?’”
Notice it doesn’t say our  or their  helper.
It says “my helper.”
We love Jehovah.
We can also be absolutely convinced
that Jehovah loves us and will help us individually.
At times, it can be difficult to trust that Jehovah loves us personally
and will act in our behalf.
What can help build our trust in Jehovah’s love?
Let’s discuss three ways.
First, Proverbs 15
—Proverbs 15, notice verse 9:
“Jehovah detests the way of the wicked one,
but he loves the one who pursues righteousness.”
“He loves the one
who pursues [or, chases after] righteousness.”
He knows we can’t be perfectly righteous.
But he loves us for trying our best,
as he said, ‘for pursuing righteousness.’
He loves us because we don’t quit.
We can trust that he’ll never abandon us
because we don’t give up in pursuing righteousness.
Second, pour out your heart to Jehovah.
Lamentations 2:19 says this
—Lamentations 2:19:
“Pour out your heart like water
before the face of Jehovah.”
It doesn’t say, “Pour out your mind” or “your thoughts”
but “pour out your heart”
—that includes our feelings, our concerns, our anxieties.
We pour out our heart like one pours out water
—not holding anything back.
When we express to our heavenly Father
our love and appreciation for him,
when we tell him our concerns and desires,
and when we ask for his direction,
we show that we value our friendship with him.
What will be the result for you?
The more you pour out your heart like water
and feel his personal response to you,
the more you’ll sense his love for you
and the more you’ll trust that he’ll never abandon you.
Your gratitude for Jehovah’s enduring love will increase.
And, third, remember that trials
do not mean a loss of Jehovah’s favor.
Our enemy knows that feeling close to Jehovah
is the source of our strength.
So he’ll try to undermine our confidence,
and he hopes that we break away from Jehovah.
For example, when Job was undergoing a severe trial,
his false comforters lyingly said that the reason for these trials
was that he’d lost Jehovah’s favor.
Jehovah reminded Job to look at creation
and to see His love and wisdom.
How did faithful Job respond?
He said at Job 42:5:
“My ears have heard about you,
but now I do see you with my eyes.”
We may wonder if we’ve lost Jehovah’s favor.
We should ask Jehovah to help us see him
and see his loyal love for us every day.
Ask him to help you use this trial
as a stepping stone to love and trust him even more.
We’ve discussed one way we get ready for the upcoming events
—build our trust that Jehovah has loyal love for us individually.
Trusting that Jehovah will never abandon us
gives us the strength to keep up the fight
and keep on the watch.
At Ephesians 6:16,
faith, or trust, in Jehovah is compared to a shield
—a shield “with which you [can] extinguish all the wicked one’s burning arrows,”
or all of Satan’s spiritual attacks.
For example, when we hear lies about Jehovah,
his organization, and those he’s appointed to take the lead,
we will not be shaken.
We won’t give up or give out.
We know the prophecy at Matthew 24:45 has been fulfilled.
Jehovah has lovingly provided a slave
who’s “faithful and discreet.”
We recognize that Jehovah provides spiritual food and direction
through this body of men at the right time.
We’re not left floundering or trying to find our way.
Therefore, we remain obedient
and responsive to the direction we receive.
We never dismiss it,
even if it doesn’t appear practical from a human standpoint.
Trusting in Jehovah’s loyal love
has saved his people in the past.
At 2 Chronicles 20:1, 2,
it tells us that Jehoshaphat learned that a coalition of nations
—“a large crowd . . . from the region of the sea”—
were coming against him.
Jehoshaphat already had the habit of turning to Jehovah.
“He resolved to search for Jehovah.”
How did he and his faithful subjects do this?
Jehoshaphat poured his heart out like water to Jehovah.
Notice in verse 12
how he expresses his complete trust in Jehovah:
“For we are powerless before this large crowd that is coming against us;
“and we do not know what we should do,
but our eyes are toward you.”
How did Jehovah respond?
Notice verse 15.
Jehovah sent Jahaziel to reassure them:
“Do not be afraid or be terrified because of this large crowd,
for the battle is not yours but God’s.”
The strategy that Jehoshaphat followed
didn’t seem practical from a human standpoint.
Jehoshaphat appointed singers
dressed “in holy adornment” to praise Jehovah.
And how unusual that he put them in front of the armed men!
Were they singing songs about how Jehovah
defeated their enemies in past wars?
No.
They sang about Jehovah’s loyal love.
What was the result?
Jehovah confused their enemies, and they attacked each other.
What lessons can we learn from this account?
Trusting Jehovah includes trusting his representatives.
The lifesaving direction we receive from Jehovah’s organization
may not appear practical from a human standpoint.
But we recognize the fulfillment  of the prophecy
at Matthew 24:45
about “the faithful and discreet slave,”
and we’re ready to obey any instruction they provide.
Yes, getting ready includes building trust
and being convinced that Jehovah will deliver us from the wicked one.
Trusting Him will help us understand
the prophetic role of “the faithful and discreet slave”
during this time of the end when Jehovah is using them
to provide lifesaving direction.
This direction is helping us to stay ready.
Jehovah has sustained us in the past,
and he sustains us now.
Seeing these things happening
can also fortify and strengthen us.
Many of you have been fighting to “keep on the watch”
for many years.
Now the end is clearly in sight.
We don’t want to give up now.
Notice the reassurance at Galatians 6:9
—Galatians 6:9:
“So let us not give up in doing what is fine,
“for in due time we will reap
if we do not tire out.”
Because of our imperfect flesh
and the efforts of Satan and this wicked world,
we must constantly battle negative influences.
Some of you dear brothers and sisters must fight hard every day
to maintain your relationship with Jehovah.
Don’t give up!
Your fight has not been in vain.
You’ve made the right choices.
Jehovah has seen your loyal love for him,
and he treasures your devotion.
Time and time again, you’ve made sacrifices
and left your comfort zone to give Jehovah your best,
to stay active in the ministry, to keep taking in spiritual food,
and to teach your children how to speak about Jehovah.
Jehovah loves you dearly for this
and will loyally continue to help you until the battle is won.
Do not give up now!
And you young ones, Jehovah loves you too.
He knows that you’re growing up in a world that’s broken.
He knows that it can be hard for you to maintain hope for the future.
Please, never forget that your God,
your heavenly Father, loves you dearly.
Never forget that your future is bright.
Whether we’re young or old or in between,
we will not give up.
We’re so close.
We see these things happening with our own eyes.
So we’ll keep on the watch, we’ll trust Jehovah with all our hearts,
we’ll trust Jehovah’s arrangements,
and we will not give out in our spiritual battle,
because we will reap rich blessings soon—very soon.
Can you believe it’s been ten years
since JW Broadcasting began?
That’s 120 monthly programs!
These programs have unified
and strengthened Jehovah’s organization.
In the next video, we’ll be reminded of some gems we’ve received
and we’ll hear personal stories that illustrate the impact
JW Broadcasting has had on the brotherhood.
We warmly welcome you,
dear brothers and sisters,
for our first
JW Broadcasting® monthly program.
“Christian neutrality.”
Modesty.
“Do the Math.”
“Deal With Anxiety One Day at a Time.”
“[Children] are an inheritance from Jehovah.”
Jehovah loves each one of us
despite our appearances or imperfections.
A marriage that has good patterns shaped by Jehovah’s principles
looks like this well-balanced family circle.
Though we’re tainted with sin,
Jehovah does not discard imperfect humans.
We may worry about what might seem to be big tests,
only to find that they’re not as overwhelming
as we feared they would be.
Each individual grain of sand reveals distinct beauty. . . .
That is how Jehovah sees each of you.
My personal favorite thing
about JW Broadcasting
has to be that there are videos
on really anything,
whether it’s something to help me in school
or something to help me in my spiritual life.
We like to theme our family worship.
Recently, we did a family worship on neutrality.
And we found a lot of great videos that specifically had to do with that.
I use my device quite a bit,
and I don’t like it to get in the way
of schoolwork and family time.
So the video has really helped me
manage my screen time so it doesn’t get in the way of those things.
Being able to see brothers and sisters
from all over the world, all different ages, all different backgrounds
serving Jehovah
—it’s helped me personally.
But I think it’s really helped the kids in setting their own spiritual goals
and being able to see
that there’s so much that can be done in Jehovah’s organization,
no matter what their interests are, and that Jehovah can take care of them.
We feel part of Jehovah’s worldwide organization.
And, you know, at the end of the broadcast, they say, “We love you, friends.”
There’s really no substitute for that.
As a special pioneer,
the pandemic lasted so long.
And I had various sources of stress.
But, fortunately, it was the direction
from the discreet slave, a motherlike organization,
that gave us direction every step of the way.
That was great.
The Governing Body taught us principles
and gave us so much support.
It’s been such a joy to hear in the Governing Body updates
that many inactive ones are coming back.
I visited a single brother who was inactive for 24 years.
And he said several times how he wanted to come back.
I was really happy that I acted
on the message from the Governing Body updates.
It really strengthened my faith.
In one Governing Body update from 2022,
they highlighted our return to the in-person ministry.
I felt like a brand-new publisher
when we went out in the field ministry again.
I felt like a baby, a toddler, in a way.
So my wife and I prayed a lot to Jehovah
for us to be able to have good conversations
and to be able to muster up the courage needed.
When we actually went from house to house,
to our surprise, householders were willing to listen.
We felt the support of the holy spirit
and felt the kindness and help from the Governing Body
during the pandemic.
So this gives us the motivation to overcome
any obstacle in our way, no matter what the future holds.
I’m really appreciative of that.
I got baptized when I was 25 years old.
What contributed to me becoming inactive
was the lack of Bible study,
neglecting my meeting attendance,
and some bad associations.
I remained inactive for ten years.
The JW Broadcasting program that helped me to return to Jehovah
was the program from February 2016,
where we find the experience of Brother Derrick,
who similarly had strayed away from Jehovah.
But he recognized that he had made a big mistake,
which caused him many problems.
So I could relate to Brother Derrick.
And so, I said,
“Why can’t I return to Jehovah?”
That video helped me fix matters
and get close to Jehovah little by little.
We’ve been able to watch Gilead School talks
and some broadcasts as a family.
It has helped us to expand our friendships
with our brothers in the congregation.
I remember a Gilead School talk that was given by Brother David Splane
with the theme “If You Look for It, You Will Find It.”
That taught us that when we want to expand our friendships
with our brothers in the congregation,
we should not focus on their defects,
but we should look more at their good qualities.
So that helped us as a family
to remain united with all those in the congregation.
I really like everything that comes out on JW Broadcasting.
But what I love the most
are the experiences of our brothers and sisters
who remain steadfast and keep their faith in Jehovah.
I love family worship so much
because we get to sit down as a family
and practice some Kingdom songs,
read a Bible story, or watch the broadcast for the month.
The first time I went to a convention of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
it was like ten thousand people.
When I went in there and I saw
all these different faces and different colors,
it was like Jehovah showing me: “Hey, Rafika,
“remember you were asking me about all different people getting together
“and being one?
See, I’m not partial; they do get along; we are unified.”
To know that you have a heavenly Father
who cares about you
—that was the best feeling on earth.
I never thought that God had a name.
And ever since that day on, I never forget Jehovah’s name.
It’s superglued in my heart.
Our love for Jehovah
and our determination to live by his standards
are being tested each day.
And yet, because we’re being well-fed spiritually,
we have everything we need to meet those tests with joy.
Dear brothers and sisters,
please be assured
of the warm love
of the Governing Body and our prayers in your behalf.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.
What program was special to you?
Do you remember one?
We encourage you to rewatch the spiritual food
that’s been presented in past programs.
And we thank Jehovah for making all this possible.
Have you ever watched the news and thought: ‘Is this it?
Is this the beginning of the great tribulation?’
In a previous episode of Apply Bible Principles,
James and Linda learned to change their focus and maintain joy.
Now they’ll help a young brother do the same.
We can’t control when the end will come,
but we can control who we are when it does.
Maybe like Thulani, you wonder if the sacrifices you made were worth it.
Francis Páez del Rosario
made sacrifices as an accomplished musician
to focus on the Kingdom.
Her life story was featured in the August 2005 Awake!
Let’s see how she views her choices in the next segment.
My dad sold the house to buy musical instruments
so that us children could become great artists.
And we achieved just that.
We made it to the top.
My dancing style became so famous
that they would advertise with only a picture of me.
Wherever they put that image,
everyone knew Los Rosario would be there.
I really liked dancing. I loved it.
I loved the makeup, the clothes, the stage.
That was me.
But after the concerts were over,
I felt empty.
That’s nothing like the happiness that comes from knowing
you’re doing what’s right before Jehovah.
That happiness doesn’t fade,
and it will always be there because it comes from Jehovah.
When I decided to leave the group,
my dad was not pleased.
He had worked so hard for it.
Things got, um,
difficult.
This opposition really pained me
because my dad and I had always enjoyed a beautiful friendship.
We were very close.
Despite the way he treated us, we never disrespected him.
We were always kind to him.
And because of that,
little by little he started to soften.
One day, one of my sons asked,
“Why don’t you invite him to a meeting?”
My dad’s eyes lit up, and he said,
“I’ve been wanting to go for some time now.”
And we started studying with him.
He knew that he had found the truth.
He enrolled in the school; he gave his first part.
So the truth really touched him deeply.
I asked him one day during the study:
“Dad, tell me, what do you think now?
“Do you think I made a good decision in leaving the group
“and following this path
and dedicating my life to Jehovah?”
He looked at me and said:
“You did well.
“You made a very good decision.
I only wish I had been able to raise all of you in the truth.”
Dad saw his children succeed, accomplish so much,
and see their dreams come true.
But he realized that that wasn’t everything.
He realized that true happiness
comes from serving the Creator, Jehovah God.
It reminded me of the words of the apostle Paul
at Philippians 3:8.
He said that he considered what he did before
“as a lot of refuse.”
We felt the same.
We were willing to leave everything behind.
After a concert, there was that emptiness inside.
It’s so different to the way I feel
after a meeting with the brothers and sisters
or after I give a Bible study
or after a day serving at Bethel with Roberto, my husband.
That happiness doesn’t go away.
There’s nothing better than that.
Francis doesn’t focus on what could’ve been
but on the blessings of the present.
She’s seen the seeds of truth take root within her family
and now happily serves as a commuter
at the Dominican Republic branch with her husband.
She isn’t the only one who followed this successful formula.
Let’s see who else from the Bible
followed the same pattern in this morning worship.
Our Scripture text and article highlight
the importance of submission
and why we should submit to Jehovah.
Of course, we find it a pleasure
to submit to Jehovah because we love him.
That’s why we submit to Jehovah.
But there is that occasion when submitting to Jehovah is difficult.
It’s hard.
Perhaps we have to take a firm stand in front of opposers.
We have to stand up for Jehovah.
That means we stick out from the world.
That’s hard.
Or perhaps we have to change something in our personal life
to bring our life more in harmony with Jehovah’s will and standards.
That’s hard.
Or perhaps we want to give wholehearted support
to an organizational adjustment or arrangement
that we don’t fully understand.
That may be hard.
So, what can help us?
Confidence that God is with his people.
If we know that God is with his people, with us,
then we know he will bless us.
Each time we’re going to make any adjustment in our life
or submit to Jehovah’s way of doing things, we’re going to get a blessing.
Can we have such confidence?
Absolutely.
In fact, we can say that Jehovah gives us signs,
or solid evidence, that he is with us.
For example, let’s open our Bibles
to Isaiah chapter 7.
Let’s go back in time
and review this historical account in Isaiah chapter 7.
The background is in verses 1 and 2,
during the days of King Ahaz.
Let’s see what we can learn.
“Now in the days of Ahaz son of Jotham son of Uzziah, the king of Judah,
“King Rezin of Syria
“and Pekah son of Remaliah, the king of Israel,
“came up to wage war against Jerusalem,
“but he could not capture it.
“A report was made to the house of David:
“‘Syria has joined forces with Ephraim.’
“And the heart of Ahaz and the heart of his people
began to tremble, like the trees of the forest shaking in the wind.”
Well, it’s true; the situation was terrifying.
Both the king of Israel and the king of Syria joined forces.
They declared war on Judah.
Why?
They wanted to dethrone Ahaz as the king
and replace him with another man, perhaps one who was not in the line of David.
Well, what a triumph that would be for Satan if he could install
his own diabolical dynasty on the throne in Jerusalem!
Would Jehovah allow that?
What did Ahaz do? What effect did it have on him?
Did he show faith and confidence in Jehovah?
He began to tremble in fear.
Verse 2 says tremble in fear,
“like the trees of the forest shaking in the wind”—no faith at all.
So, what does Jehovah do?
Well, verse 11,
Jehovah continued speaking to Ahaz:
“Ask for a sign from Jehovah . . . ;
[make it] as deep as the Grave or as high as the sky.”
‘Ahaz, just ask for a sign.
I want to help you.’
And what does Ahaz say?
‘No, I’m not going to ask for a sign.’
So Jehovah says: ‘What?
‘You’re not going to ask for a sign?
Well, I’m going to give you a sign.’
And that’s in verse 14:
“Therefore, Jehovah himself will give you a sign:
“Look! The young woman will become pregnant
“and will give birth to a son,
and she will name him Immanuel.”
Jehovah assures Ahaz
that He will protect the line of David,
not just with words, notice, but with a sign.
‘You’re going to have this son.
You’re going to see a boy named Immanuel.’
And that name is not just random.
The name means something.
The name means “With Us Is God.”
‘Ahaz, with us is God.
‘I’m not going to allow the covenant that I made with David to be broken.
Ahaz, I don’t tell lies,’ Jehovah says.
‘I don’t tell lies to David’ (Psalm 89:35)
—a sign.
What happens?
Verse 16, Jehovah gets more specific:
“Before the boy knows how to reject the bad and choose the good,
“the land of the two kings whom you dread
will be completely abandoned.”
So, notice, that’s exactly what happened.
The birth of Immanuel held true,
and before the boy was old enough to know between good and bad,
those two kings, Pekah and Rezin, were killed.

Why?
Because God is with his people.
That’s the lesson: Immanuel.

And what a warning this is for all of us and for all of those
who want to try to oppose Jehovah’s way of doing things!

There’s no conspiracy that can win
or somehow interrupt Jehovah’s purpose.
Verse 10 says:

—a warning to all those who oppose Jehovah.
In the days of Hezekiah, you had the Assyrians—185,000 Assyrians.

you’re going to die.’—185,000 died.
Why?
Because clearly God is with his people and the royal line of David.
No conspiracy will succeed.
So, what does this mean for you and me?
What does this mean for us?
Does it have meaning?
Can we have confidence that God is with us today?
Now let’s open our Bibles to Matthew 1:23,
Matthew 1:23.
Here we have now the angel speaking to Joseph about the birth of Jesus.
But notice what he says in verse 23:
“‘Look! The virgin will become pregnant and will give birth to a son,
“‘and they will name him Immanuel’ [there it is again],

Do we see the connection?
The name Immanuel comes up again,
and this time it represents Christ Jesus
—his role, his leadership, his rulership—
the title given to Jesus.
Do we see the connection?
The prophecy about Immanuel is completely fulfilled in Jesus.
He rules as our heavenly King.
And because of the blessing and the protection of his rulership,
we have every reason to declare with confidence today,
“With us is God.”
Do you see the signs?
Do you see the evidence that Jehovah is giving us to prove he is with us?
Do you see Jesus living up to that wonderful name, Immanuel?
For example,
several weeks ago, we had a report from the Writing Committee.
And despite the obstacles of the past year —do you recall that report?—
the work in the Writing Department, Art Department,
MEPS, Text Processing, and Translation Services didn’t stop.
It didn’t even slow down.
Bible translations in 2019, 33 were released;
in 2020, 33 were released.
Add the comments from Wednesday about a country
that is now having more and more Bible studies
and an increase in interested ones and baptisms
—these are more than just updates.
These are more than just statistics.
Do we see them as evidences
that “with us is God”
and that he is backing us up in our undertakings?
That’s what we want to understand.
No, we’re not perfect.
We’ll get there at the end of the Thousand Year Reign.
But compare the leadership and rulership
of Immanuel, Christ Jesus, with the world’s leadership.
Look what we have.
It’s wonderful to contemplate.
So, what’s the lesson for you and me?
Don’t miss the clear evidence that God is with us.
Keep your spiritual vision sharp and clear.
So here’s a tip.
After reading a portion of the Bible,
ask yourself: ‘How did Jehovah
‘keep his word in this situation?
How does this show God is with us today?’

into your own life and personal circumstances.
Build your confidence in the situation that you are in.

we are convinced that he will bless us every time
we have to bring ourselves into submission to Jehovah.

Jehovah assured him that He would protect the line of David,
not just with words, but with a sign:
a boy, Immanuel, “With Us Is God.”
Today, Jesus, in his role as Immanuel, rules as our heavenly King.
And because of the blessing of his rulership,
we have every reason to declare with confidence: “With us is God.”
The sign of Immanuel is all around us.
The question is, Do we see and appreciate the evidence?
Jehovah has never abandoned his servants,
and he will not start with you.
Keep looking for the evidence that he is with you now.

This month’s postcard comes from Malaysia,
a Southeast Asian country renowned for its diversity.
There are quiet farmlands,
bustling cities,
densely packed forests, and calming coastlines.
You’ll find a wide variety of creatures like pygmy elephants,
proboscis monkeys,
and rhinoceros hornbills.
Malaysia is home to wide ethnic diversity,
displaying an amazing variety of clothing,
languages, and delicious foods.
Missionaries arrived in the country in the 1930’s,
and the truth began to spread.
In the early 1950’s, the first congregation was formed.
Some of the missionaries conducted 15 Bible studies a month.
Our brothers and sisters still find many righthearted people.
The over 5,000 publishers
average almost one Bible study per publisher!
Many studies are conducted in longhouses,
a collection of simple family homes near the water,
combined together and raised with stilts.
Proverbs 9:3 says:
“[Wisdom sends] out its female servants to call out from the heights above.”
You might say the sisters in Malaysia take that verse literally,
preaching high on Mount Kinabalu
and across cable bridges stretched over the forest.
The 89 publishers of the Keningau Congregation
send their warm love and greetings to you all.
From the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

en.text: “He still speaks through his faith.”
Whoa!
Have you read about Abel?
Even after 6,000 years,
he still speaks to us through his faithful example.
That’s incredible,
especially considering his living situation.
A lot of family drama!
C’mon, let’s take a look at that account.
Abel’s parents were Adam and Eve.
They disobeyed Jehovah
and had to leave the Paradise that God made for them.
Abel also had a brother named Cain.
He was angry and violent.
Abel’s family were bad examples of faith.
So how did Abel build his faith?
Well, there were cherubs who guarded the way to the garden
where his parents used to live.
Abel could see other creatures who had faith in Jehovah,
so he wasn’t alone.
Abel could enjoy the beautiful things Jehovah made
and know God loved him.
And Abel could think about Jehovah’s promise
and hope that someday he’d live in Paradise.
Even though Abel had a family who did not love Jehovah,
he still saw and heard plenty to help him build faith in God.
That helped Abel become Jehovah’s friend.
Why not read Abel’s story
and let his account speak to you.
Make time every day to learn from Jehovah’s friends.
What do you think?
How did Abel show
that he was Jehovah’s friend?
How did Abel build his faith in Jehovah?
How can you build your faith?

이 대회들의 최고 참석자수는 도합 9만 8000명이 넘고,

그런데 놀랍게도 최고 참석자수는 2만 8617명이나 되었습니다!
분명 발전 가능성이 아주 높습니다.
사실 이 대회에서만 293명이 침례를 받았습니다!
파라과이의 신권 역사상 한 장소에서 가장 많은 수가 침례를 받은 것이죠.
정말 여호와께서는 이 대회들을 축복하셨습니다.
올해 2개의 대회가 더 남아 있고,
2025년에는 19개의 특별 지역 대회가 열리게 될 것입니다.

이 판결은 환자 각자가 자기가 받을 치료를 선택할 수 있는 기본 권리를 확증해 주었습니다.
이 결정이 특히 중요했던 이유는
이것이 유럽 인권 재판소 대재판부에서 내린 판결이기 때문입니다.
대재판부는 여러 나라에 영향을 미칠 수 있는 사건들만 다룹니다.
따라서 이번 결정에 따라 유럽의 46개 국가는
환자가 자신의 치료를 선택할 권리를 존중해야 합니다.
우리는 대재판부의 판결에 감사합니다.
무엇보다도 여호와께 감사드리죠.
이번 법적 승리는
유럽에 있는 모든 형제 자매들이 의료상의 결정을 내릴 때 큰 도움이 될 것입니다.
이 중요한 판결로 무엇을 알 수 있습니까?
우리가 선택한 치료법을 의사와 상의하고
서면으로 남겨야 한다는 거죠.
무야 자매가 그랬던 것처럼요.
이번 달인 2024년 9월에
우리는 「행복한 삶을 영원히 누리십시오!」 팜플렛을 사용해 성서 연구를 시작하는
세계적인 활동에 참여하고 있습니다.
전 세계에 있는 우리 형제 자매들과 연합해 이 활동을 함께하는 것은 정말 기쁜 일이죠!
경험담을 좀 소개해 드리겠습니다.
오스트리아에 사는 하넬로레는 84세 된 파이오니아 자매입니다.
자매는 건강이 좋지 않아 오랫동안 호별 봉사를 할 수 없죠.
그래서 자매는 이전에 방문했을 때 좋은 반응을 보였던 사람들에게
성서 연구를 제안해 보기로 했습니다.
6명을 생각해 내서 방문했죠.
자매는 여섯 명 모두에게 성서 연구하는 법을 보여 줄 수 있어서 기뻤습니다.
어떻게 됐을까요?
여섯 명 모두 성서 연구를 계속하기로 했습니다.
필리핀에서 호별 봉사를 하던 두 전도인은
아파트 앞에서 빨래를 하던 조시라는 여자에게 말을 건넸습니다.
조시는 바빴기 때문에 자기 말고 안에 있는 성인인 아들과 조카에게 말해 보라고 했습니다.
전도인들은 그 아들과 조카에게 성서 연구를 직접 제안했고,
바로 그 자리에서 연구가 시작되었습니다.
성서 연구하는 법을 보여 주고 있는데
조시의 조카딸이 대화에 참여했습니다.
그래서 전도인들은 연구를 제안했고 조카딸은 즉시 받아들였죠.
세 명이 그렇게 성서 연구를 하고 있는 모습을 보고
조시도 호기심이 생겼고
그래서 대화에 참여하기 시작했습니다.
조시도 성서 연구를 받아들였죠.
그런데 그 두 전도인이 성서 연구를 마치기 전에
다섯 번째로 조시의 딸이 도대체 무슨 이야기를 하고 있는 거냐고 물었습니다.
그 기회를 놓치지 않고 전도인들은 조시의 딸에게도 성서 연구를 제안했고
그는 즉시 받아들였습니다.
결국 5명의 사람이 한 집에서 성서 연구를 받아들였습니다.
직접 제안하는 방식으로 그렇게 된 거죠.
분명 여호와께서는 이 특별 기간에 성서 연구를 제안하는 우리의 노력을 축복하고 계십니다.
하지만 우리는 계속해서 이 일에 노력을 기울이기 원합니다.
형제 자매 여러분,
특별 활동이 끝나도 열정을 잃지 말고 계속 힘차게 이 일을 하십시오.
계속 성서 연구를 가능한 모든 기회에 제안하십시오.
그럼 무엇이 도움이 될까요?
물론 공개 증거가 우리의 봉사의 중요한 부면이고
그렇게 해서 성서 연구가 생기기도 하지만,
모두가 호별 봉사에 정기적으로 참여하도록 권해드립니다.
그리고 사람들이 집에 있을 가능성이 높을 때에 방문하면 더 좋은 결과가 있을 겁니다.
그렇게 하면 성서 연구로 이어질 대화를 시작할 기회가 더 많이 생길 수 있습니다.
적절한 경우 연구를 직접 제안해 보시기 바랍니다.
독일의 한 형제는 어느 날
저녁에 봉사를 하다가 35살쯤 된 남자와 대화를 했습니다.
형제가 물었죠.
“언제 마지막으로 성경을 읽으셨나요?”
남자는 말했죠.
“오늘 아침에요.”
미가 4:3, 4을 사용해서 그들은 성경이 왜 가치 있는 책인지 대화를 나누었습니다.
그리고 「행복한 삶을 영원히 누리십시오!」 팜플렛 1과를 토의했죠.
그 자리에 있던 그 남자의 자녀들이 성구들을 소리 내어 읽었습니다.
남자는 성서 연구를 시작하기로 했죠.
또한 많은 분들은 비공식 증거를 통해 성서 연구를 시작했습니다.
친척, 이웃, 직장 동료, 가게 주인 등에게 증거했죠.
탄자니아의 엘리자베스라는 자매는 4건이나 되는 성서 연구를
특별 활동 기간 초반에 시작했습니다.
그중 한 사람은 왕국회관 건너에 있는 작은 카페의 여주인이었죠.
엘리자베스는 그곳에 자주 들러서
차나 작은 소품들을 사곤 했는데,
그 주인에게 성서 연구를 직접 제안해 보기로 했습니다.
그들은 「즐겁게 성경을 공부해 보세요」 동영상을 보았고, 여주인은 기뻐하며 이렇게 말했죠.
“지금 당장 시작해요!”
그러고는 자기 딸과 조카딸도 불러서 연구하는 걸 보게 했죠.
그 여자가 집회도 참석했기 때문에 엘리자베스는 정말 기뻤습니다.
집회가 어땠냐고 물어보자 여자가 대답했죠.
“저는 여호와의 증인의 이런 점이 정말 좋아요.
성경을 공부하잖아요.
다른 교회에 가 보면, 그냥 노래하고 설교만 하지
성경은 공부하지 않아요.
그게 정말 달라요.
전 여기에 계속 올 거예요.”
이런 훌륭한 경험들을 들으면 정말 힘이 납니다.
우린 봉사에 사용하는 소중한 시간을
지혜롭게 사용하길 원합니다.
고린도 전서 9:26은 이러합니다.
“그러므로 나는 목표 없이 달리지 않습니다.
주먹을 뻗어 허공을 치지도 않습니다.”
우리는 여호와께 가장 좋은 것을 드리고 싶습니다.
정기적으로 호별 방문을 하는 것에 더해 또 무엇이 도움이 될 수 있습니까?
어떤 구역에서는 전도인들이 재방문을 많이 합니다.
하지만 우리의 재방문이 생산적인지
기도하면서 생각해 볼 필요가 있습니다.
진리에 대한 그들의 사랑이 자라고 있습니까?
우리의 방문을 정말 고마워합니까?
그들은 성서 연구에 관심이 있습니까?
그게 아니라면 우린 ‘허공을 치고 있는’ 것일지 모릅니다.
우리의 노력을 다른 곳으로 기울여야 할 때죠.
그런 사람들은 구역을 다시 돌 때 좋은 소식을 들을 기회가 또 있을 것입니다.
물론 균형과 참을성과 분별력이 필요합니다.
중요한 건 우리의 시간을 잘 활용해야 한다는 겁니다.
그와 비슷하게 성서 연구생이 잘 발전하고 있는지도 자문해 보아야 합니다.
기도하면서 생각해 보십시오.
‘그들은 성경 진리를 받아들이는가?
배우는 점을 적용하고 필요한 변화를 하고 있는가?
회중 집회들에 참석하기 시작했는가?
배운 것을 다른 사람들에게 이야기하는가?’
연구생이 발전하지 않는다면,
‘영원한 생명을 얻기에 합당한 사람들’을 찾는 데 시간과 활력을 쓰는 것이 더 나을 것입니다.
형제 자매 여러분, 계속 모든 기회에 성서 연구를 제안하도록 합시다!
세계 여러 지역에서 성서 연구가 증가하고 있고,
많은 사람이 침례를 받고 있습니다.
예를 들어, 최근에 마다가스카르에서 열린 한 대회에는
2만 1000명이 넘게 참석했고
419명이 침례를 받았습니다.
또한 필리핀에서는 2024 봉사 연도 중에
5퍼센트의 증가가 있었습니다.
어떤 일이 있었죠?
처음으로 전도인 수가 26만 명을 넘어서게 되었습니다.
성서 연구 수가 25만 2000건을 넘어섰고,
이 봉사 연도에 침례를 받은 사람만 1만 2201명이었습니다.
120개의 새로운 회중과 15개의 새로운 순회구가 생겼죠!
대단합니다!
어디에 살고 있든, 우리는 요한 4:35의 예수의 말씀을 떠올리게 됩니다.
“눈을 들어 밭을 보십시오.
희어져 수확하게 되었습니다.”
또한 예수께서는 마태 9:37, 38에서 제자들에게 이렇게 말씀하셨습니다.
“참으로, 수확할 것은 많은데 일꾼은 적습니다.
그러므로 수확하는 주인에게 수확할 일꾼들을 보내 달라고 청하십시오.”
분명 전 세계 여러 지역의 밭이 “희어져 수확하게 되었습니다.”
따라서 이런 질문이 생깁니다.
우리 각자는 어떻게 전파하고 가르치는 일에 더 많이 참여할 수 있습니까?
물론 우리 각자의 상황은 다릅니다.
그렇지만 보조 파이오니아로 봉사할 기회를 찾아 볼 수 있습니까?
혹시 정규 파이오니아로 봉사할 수 있습니까?
이미 파이오니아를 하고 있다면
더 크게 필요한 곳에서 심지어 외국에서 봉사할 수 있습니까?
여러분은 왕국 전파자 학교에 지원하려는 생각을 해 본 적이 있습니까?
이 학교를 졸업한 사람들은 임시 특별 파이오니아,
특별 파이오니아,
순회 감독자,
선교인으로 봉사하기도 합니다.
우리 각자의 상황이 어떠하든,
여호와의 봉사에서 더 많이 섬길 수 있는 기회가 우리에겐 정말 많이 있습니다.
「여호와의 뜻을 행하는 조직」 책 10장에서는
봉사의 직무를 확장할 수 있는 여러 방법을 소개합니다.
우리가 이러한 방법으로 여호와를 시험한다면
분명 그분의 축복을 받을 것입니다.
요약해 볼까요?
특별 활동에서 얻은 열정을 계속 유지하십시오.
계속 모든 기회에 성서 연구를 제안하십시오.
세계의 여러 지역에서 놀라운 증가가 이루어지고 있다는 점도 살펴봤습니다.
계속해서 ‘주인에게 수확할 일꾼들을 [더 많이] 보내 달라고’ 기도해야겠습니다.
우리 각자도 “왕국의 좋은 소식”을 전파하고 가르치기 위해 계속 최선을 다합시다.
잊지 마십시오.
우리는 여러분 한 사람 한 사람을 정말 소중히 여깁니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome, brothers and sisters!
Since our last report,
we’ve had seven more special conventions.
They were held in Philadelphia, United States;
Sofia, Bulgaria;
Suva, Fiji;
Lyon, France;
Asunción, Paraguay;
Tampa, United States;
and Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.
More than 16,000 delegates
traveled from 101 countries
to attend these conventions.
There was a combined peak attendance
of over 98,000.
And 859 were baptized.
In Paraguay, there are currently about 11,500 publishers.
Nearly 2,000 delegates
were invited to attend the special convention.
Remarkably, though, the peak attendance
Clearly, there’s much potential for growth.
In fact,
293 were baptized at this convention alone!
That’s the largest baptism at one location in the history
of our work in Paraguay.
Jehovah has truly blessed these special conventions.
Two more remain for 2024,
and we look forward to 19 special conventions
for the 2025 series.
Here’s a brief legal update.
On September 17, 2024,
the 17 judges
of the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights
ruled in favor of Sister Pindo Mulla,
who was given blood transfusions in Spain against her wishes.
Despite our sister’s clear oral and written refusal,
a judge in Spain allowed doctors to proceed.
The Grand Chamber concluded that this violated her rights.
It confirmed that patients have the fundamental right
to choose their own medical care.
What makes this decision especially significant
is that it was issued by the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights.
The Grand Chamber issues decisions
only when a case is considered to be groundbreaking.
Thus, this decision obligates 46 countries in Europe
to respect patients’ health-care choices.
We’re grateful to the Grand Chamber for this decision.
Above all, we thank Jehovah for this legal victory,
which will benefit all of our brothers and sisters in Europe
as they make informed medical decisions.
This significant ruling reminds us how vital it is
to discuss our personal medical choices with our doctor
and to put these choices in writing, just as our faithful sister did.
During this month, September 2024,
we’ve all been involved in a global campaign to start Bible studies
using the Enjoy Life Forever!  brochure.
What a joy to be united with our brothers and sisters worldwide
in this campaign!
Note a couple of experiences.
Hannelore is an 84-year-old pioneer sister in Austria.
Because of her health, she can’t preach from door to door
for long periods of time.
However, she decided to offer a Bible course
to people who had responded positively to her visits before.
She thought of six people and visited them.
She was very happy to demonstrate the Bible course
with all six people.
The result?
All six agreed to continue the course in the coming days.
In the Philippines, while witnessing from house to house,
two publishers approached a woman named Josie
who was doing laundry in front of her apartment.
Since Josie was busy, she told the publishers to talk instead
to her adult son and nephew who were inside.
Using the direct approach, the publishers started a Bible study right away
with both the son and the nephew.
As the Bible study was being demonstrated,
Josie’s niece also joined in the discussion
and the publishers offered her a Bible study,
which she readily accepted.
Now with three persons involved in the initial Bible study session,
Josie became more curious
and also wanted to join in the conversation.
Josie too accepted a Bible study.
However, before the two publishers ended the initial study session,
a fifth family member, Josie’s daughter,
was moved to ask what they were discussing.
Taking advantage of yet another opportunity,
the publishers offered her a Bible study, which she immediately accepted.
In all, five family members from one household
accepted the offer to have a Bible study using the direct approach.
Clearly, Jehovah has blessed our efforts
to offer Bible studies during the campaign.
But we want to continue to focus on starting Bible studies.
Brothers and sisters,
don’t lose the momentum of this campaign!
Ride the wave of enthusiasm.
Continue to offer Bible studies at every appropriate opportunity.
What can help us to do so?
Although public witnessing is an important aspect of our ministry
and Bible studies sometimes result,
we encourage all to share regularly in the house-to-house work.
And remember, we will have better results
if we call at times when people are more likely to be home.
This gives us more opportunities to start conversations
that lead to Bible studies.
Why not try the direct approach when it seems appropriate?
While sharing in the ministry one evening,
a brother in Germany spoke with a man who is about 35 years old.
The brother asked him,
“When did you last read the Bible?”
The man replied, “This morning.”
They talked about why the Bible is valuable,
using Micah 4:3, 4 as an example.
Then, they discussed lesson 01 of the Enjoy Life Forever!  brochure.
The man’s children were present and read the Bible verses aloud.
The man agreed to start the Bible course.
In addition, many have started studies
by witnessing informally to relatives,
neighbors, coworkers, shopkeepers, and so forth.
In Tanzania, a sister named Elizabeth
started four new studies during the first days of the campaign.
One was with a woman who has a small café
across the street from the Kingdom Hall.
Elizabeth frequently stopped in her shop for tea
or to purchase small items,
and she decided to offer her a study using the direct approach.
They watched the video Welcome to Your Bible Study,
and the woman was delighted.
She said, “We should start right now!”
She also included her daughter and her niece
in the demonstration of the study.
Elizabeth was so pleased
that she also attended a congregation meeting.
When asked what she thought of the meeting, the woman said:
“That’s what I love about Jehovah’s Witnesses.
“They study the Bible.
“When I go to other churches, they just sing and preach
“but don’t study the Bible.
“I really loved it.
I will try to come regularly.”
We are happy to hear these positive experiences.
Our time in the ministry is valuable,
and we want to use it wisely.
As 1 Corinthians 9:26 says:
“Therefore, the way I am running is not aimlessly;
the way I am aiming my blows is so as not to be striking the air.”
We love to give Jehovah our best.
In addition to having a regular share in the house-to-house work,
what else can help us?
In some areas, publishers have many return visits.
But perhaps we need to consider prayerfully
if our return visits are productive.
Are such individuals growing in their love of the truth?
Do they truly appreciate our visits?
Are they interested in a Bible study?
If not, perhaps we are “striking the air.”
It might be best to redirect our efforts.
Those individuals will have another opportunity to hear the good news
when the territory is worked again.
Of course, balance, patience, and discernment are needed.
But we want to be sure we are making the best use of our time.
Similarly, we might ask ourselves,
‘Are my Bible students making progress?’
Prayerfully consider:
Are they accepting Bible truths?
Are they beginning to apply what they learn
and to make changes where needed?
Have they begun to attend congregation meetings?
Are they speaking with others about what they learn?
If they are not progressing, it would be best to spend our time and energy
seeking out those who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
So brothers and sisters, let’s continue to offer Bible studies
at every opportunity!
In many places around the world,
we’re seeing an increase of Bible studies
and tremendous growth.
For example, at a recent convention in Madagascar
with over 21,000 in attendance,
419 were baptized.
Also, the Philippines reports that during the 2024 service year,
they had 5 percent growth.
What’s been the result?
For the first time, they reported more than 260,000 publishers.
The number of studies has grown to over 252,000,
and 12,201 were baptized during the service year;
120 new congregations and 15 new circuits were formed!
Amazing!
Wherever you may live,
we think of Jesus’ words at John 4:35:
“Lift up your eyes and view the fields,
that they are white for harvesting.”
Also, Jesus said to his disciples
at Matthew 9:37, 38:
“Yes, the harvest is great,
“but the workers are few.
“Therefore, beg the Master of the harvest
to send out workers into his harvest.”
The fields are certainly “white for harvesting”
in many places around the world.
Of course, that raises the question,
How can we individually expand our share
in the preaching and teaching work?
Clearly, we each have different circumstances.
But could you look for opportunities to serve
as an auxiliary pioneer?
Could you reach out and become a regular pioneer?
If you’re already pioneering, could you serve where there is a greater need,
perhaps even in another land?
Have you considered applying to attend
the School for Kingdom Evangelizers?
Some graduates of that school are used as temporary special pioneers,
special pioneers,
circuit overseers, and missionaries.
Truly, there are so many opportunities to reach out in Jehovah’s service
according to our own individual circumstances.
The book Organized to Do Jehovah’s Will, chapter 10,
discusses many ways we can expand our ministry.
If we test Jehovah out in this way,
we can be certain of his blessing.
So, what have we discussed?
Keep the momentum of our special campaign going.
Continue to offer Bible studies at every opportunity.
We also discussed the thrilling increases we’re seeing
in many parts of the world.
May we all continue to pray
that ‘the Master sends out more workers into the harvest.’
And may we continue to do our personal best
to preach and teach “the good news of the Kingdom.”
Be assured that we cherish
each and every one of you dear brothers and sisters.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.

title: 조엘 델링거: 진리 안에 머물려면 인내가 꼭 필요합니다 (디모데 후서 4:7, 8)

ko.text: 함께 성경을 펴서 디모데 후서 4:7, 8을 읽어 보겠습니다.
오늘의 성구의 문맥을 이해할 수 있게 해 주는데요.
기억나시겠지만 바울이 디모데에게 편지를 썼던 기원 65년경에
그는 로마에 있는 감옥에 투옥되어 있었죠.
사슬에 매여 죽음을 앞두고 있었습니다.
이 점을 생각해 보죠.
바울은 시련을 성공적으로 인내했습니까?
함께 디모데 후서 4:7부터 읽어 보겠습니다.
“나는 훌륭한 싸움을 싸웠고
경주를 끝까지 달렸으며 믿음을 지켰습니다.
이제는 나를 위해 의의 면류관이 예비되어 있습니다.
의로운 심판관이신 주께서 그 날에 그것을 나에게 상으로 주실 것입니다.
나에게만이 아니라, 그분이 나타나시기를 고대해 온 모든 사람에게도 주실 것입니다.”
자신이 곧 죽을 걸 알았는데도 정말 용기 있고 긍정적인 시각을 가졌죠!
바울은 여호와께 봉사를 드리면서 인내한 것이 다른 무엇보다 가치가 있다고 확신했습니다.
바울은 마태 24:13에서 예수께서 하신 이 말씀이 참되다는 걸 알았죠.
“끝까지 [자신의 삶의 끝이나, 이 세상 제도의 끝까지]
인내하는 사람은 구원을 받을 것입니다.”
바울처럼 우리 각자도 완주해야 할 경주가 있습니다.
우리 각자는 어떻게 하고 있습니까?
우린 모두 달리고 있죠.
출발했을 때보다 결승선에 더 가까워졌습니다. 기쁜 소식이죠.
하지만 점점 지치시나요?
팬데믹이나 나쁜 소식에 지치고,
이 악한 세상 제도가 끝나가면서
친구들과 가족들이 여러 면으로 고통받는 걸 보며 지치고 있습니까?
오늘 아침에는 포기하거나 지치지 않을 힘을 얻기 위해
먼저 성경에 나오는 “인내”의 의미를 생각해 보겠습니다.
그리고 사랑의 하느님이신 여호와께서 하신 위로가 되는 보증의 말씀을 살펴보죠.
우선 성경에서 인내란 무엇입니까?
이 단어에 해당하는 그리스어 명사는
“용기 있고 굳건한 혹은 참을성 있는 ‘인내’를 의미하는 말로서,
장애물이나 박해나 시련이나 유혹에 직면해서도 희망을 잃지 않는 것을 말합니다.”
정말 훌륭한 특성이죠.
관련된 동사는 흔히 도망치지 않고,
자신의 입장을 고수하고 견뎌낸다는 뜻을 갖고 있습니다.
「여호와의 뜻을 행하는 조직」 책 17장에서는 이 특성을 아름답게 묘사합니다.
나중에 읽어 보실 수 있지만 핵심이 되는 한 문장을 읽어 드리죠.
“인내하지 않고서는 진리 안에 머물러 있을 수 없습니다.”
우리가 계속 길러나가야 할 이 소중한 특성인 인내가
우리 모두에게 그토록 중요한 이유는 무엇입니까?
우리가 이 경주를 얼마나 오래 달려왔는지 상관없이 말이죠.
예를 들어 보겠습니다.
마라톤 경기에 참여하는 사람들을 생각해 보죠.
처음에는 모든 참가자들이 열심히 뜁니다.
잘하는 거죠.
하지만 결승선을 통과하기도 전에 포기하는 참가자는 어떻게 될까요?
경주를 훨씬 더 일찍 포기한 사람보다 더 나은 점이 있을까요?
아예 경주에 참가하지 않은 사람보다 나을까요?
아닙니다.
경주에서 포기하거나 지치면 결과는 같죠.
실격입니다.
상을 받지 못하게 됩니다.
요점이 뭐죠?
우리 모두는 얼마나 오랫동안 달려왔든지,
현재 얼마나 지쳐 있든지 간에
여호와의 도움으로 경주를 끝까지 달리겠다고 결심해야 합니다.
이 점을 생각하면 저는 만코카 형제에게서 들은 말이 떠오릅니다.
「연감」에서 앙골라의 신권 역사를 읽어 보셨다면 주앙 만코카 형제에 대한 내용을 보셨을 겁니다.
우리 모두는 형제가 극심한 박해 속에서 나타낸 충실함을 본받아야 합니다.
만코카 형제는 아직도 살아 계신데, 현재 95세이시죠.
충실하고 활력이 넘치는 이 형제는 현재 앙골라 지부 위원으로 섬기고 있습니다.
몇 년 전에, 저는 당시 88세이던 형제를 만날 기회가 있었습니다.
저는 형제를 격려하려고 했지만 오히려 제가 만코카 형제에게 더 많은 격려를 받았습니다.
형제가 과거에 충실했던 얘기가 나왔을 때 이렇게 말씀하셨죠.
“내가 과거에 어땠는지가 중요한 게 아니라,
지금 어떠한지가 중요합니다.”
네, 지금까지 경주를 달려온 만코카 형제와
다른 소중한 연로한 형제 자매들은 인내가 무엇인지를 아십니다.
인내란 얼마나 많고 힘든 시련을 겪든지 계속 앞으로 나아가고,
강한 희망과 긍정적인 시각을 유지하는 것임을 아시죠.
그게 우리의 목표입니다. 끝까지 인내하는 거죠.
이제 성경을 펴서 고린도 전서 10:13을 보겠습니다.
전에도 읽어 보셨겠지만 큰 위로가 되는 보증의 말씀이 나오죠.
이 말씀을 잠깐 동안 자세히 살펴보겠습니다.
그러면서 자신만이 아니라 가족이나 회중 형제 자매들 중에
이 성구를 보여 주면 유익을 얻을 만한 사람을 떠올려 보시기 바랍니다.
아마 다음 몇 주 동안
이 성구에 담긴 격려가 필요한 사람들을 생각해 볼 수 있을 것입니다.
고린도 전서 10:13입니다.
“사람들이 일반적으로 받는 유혹 외에는 아무 유혹도 여러분에게 닥치지 않습니다.
하느님은 충실하셔서,
여러분이 견딜 수 있는 것 이상으로 유혹받게 하지 않으실 것입니다.
그리고 유혹이 있을 때에 빠져나갈 길을 마련하셔서
여러분이 인내할 수 있게 해 주실 것입니다.”
이 영감받은 하느님의 말씀을 무엇이라고 요약할 수 있을까요?
앞으로 우리가 결승선에 도착하기 전에 삶에 어떤 시련이 닥치든,
여호와를 신뢰한다면 그분이 우리를 붙들어 주신다는 것입니다.
여기에는 두 가지 기본 진리가 들어 있습니다.
이 위로의 말씀의 근간을 이루는 진리죠.
첫째로, 13절 앞부분에서
우리가 겪는 시련이 “사람들이 일반적으로 받는” 것이라고 했습니다.
무슨 뜻이죠?
우리가 현재 겪고 있는 스트레스, 염려, 어려움은
모든 사람이 공통적으로 겪는 일이라는 것입니다.
따라서 여호와 하느님을 의지하는 한
우리가 견딜 수 있는 것 이상의 어려움들은 없습니다.
고린도 전서 10장의 문맥에서 특히 6-11절을 보면,
바울은 이스라엘 백성이 광야에서 직면한 시험들을 언급합니다.
그 시험들을 생각해 보십시오.
그들이 광야를 돌아다니며 40년 동안 겪은 그 어떤 시련도
사람들이 일반적으로 겪는 시련 이상의 것은 없었습니다.
다 충실한 이스라엘 사람들이 견딜 수 있는 것들이었죠.
흥미롭게도 바울은 이스라엘이 불순종한 경우를 네 번 언급합니다.
안타깝게도 일부 이스라엘 백성은 그릇된 욕망에 넘어갔는데,
그 이유는 시련들이 약한 인간이 감당하기에는 너무 벅차거나
여호와께서 돕지 않으셔서가 아니었습니다.
그들이 하느님을 의지하지 않았기 때문이었죠.
이 구절에 담긴 두 번째 진리는 무엇입니까?
“하느님은 충실하시다”고 했죠.
정말 그렇지 않습니까?
우리는 온갖 시련을 겪을 때
여호와께서 충실히 우리를 지원해 주시는 것을 경험해 왔습니다.
실제로 하느님께서 자신의 백성을 대하신 기록을 살펴보면,
그분이 충성스러운 사랑이 풍부하시고, 자신에게 순종하는 사람들에게
충성스러운 사랑을 크게 나타내신다는 점을 알게 됩니다.
여호수아가 한 것처럼
여호와께서 우리를 돌보신 기록과
그분이 이스라엘 시대 때부터 자신의 백성을 대해 오신 기록을 돌아보면 무엇을 알게 됩니까?
우리는 “여호와께서 … 하신 모든 선한 약속 중에
한 말씀도 빠지지 않고 다 이루어졌다는 것”을 알게 됩니다.
여호와께서는 오늘도 내일도
우리가 시험과 유혹에 직면할 때 충실히 도와주실 것입니다.
따라서 두 가지를 기억합시다.
(1) 여호와께서는 어떤 시련도 우리가 견디지 못할 정도까지 허용하지 않으실 겁니다.
(2) 그분은 빠져나갈 길을 마련하실 것입니다.
다양한 방법으로 여호와께서는 시련을 없애시거나
우리가 기쁨과 희망과 확신을 갖고 시련을 인내하도록 도우실 수 있습니다.
그분의 도움으로 우리 모두는 결승선을 통과할 수 있습니다.
오늘 살펴본 점들을 기억하면서 여호와를 섬기는 또 하루를 인내로 달립시다.
또 서로를 격려하고 강하게 함으로 다른 사람들도 그렇게 하도록 도웁시다.

en.text: I’d like to invite you to open up your Bible with me, please,
to 2 Timothy chapter 4,
as we’ll read verses 7 and 8,
which gives us a little context
around our day’s text.
As you may recall,
at the time Paul was writing to Timothy,
around the year 65 C.E.,
Paul was in a Roman prison,
he was in chains, and he was facing an imminent death.
The question we could ask,
Was Paul enduring his trials successfully?
Well, let’s read together 2 Timothy chapter 4 beginning in verse 7.
Paul says: “I have fought the fine fight,
“I have run the race to the finish, I have observed the faith.
“From this time on,
“there is reserved for me the crown of righteousness,
“which the Lord, the righteous judge,
“will give me as a reward in that day,
“yet not to me only,
but also to all those who have loved his manifestation.”
Well, what a courageous, positive outlook
for a man who knew he was about to die!
Paul was convinced
that his endurance in Jehovah’s service
had been well worth the effort.
He knew the truthfulness of what Jesus had earlier said
at Matthew 24:13,
that “the one who has endured to the end
“[whether it be the end of his life or the end of the system of things]
will be saved.”
Well, like Paul, each of us has a race we need to finish.
So we might ask the question, How are we doing?
Well, all of us are running.
We’re closer to the finish line than when we started.
That’s great news.
But are we getting tired
—tired of this pandemic, tired of bad news,
tired of seeing our friends and family members
suffer in various ways
as this wicked system of things comes to a close?
This morning, to strengthen us to not give up or give out,
I thought it would be good for us to first consider
the meaning of Scriptural “endurance,”
and then we’ll discuss a comforting assurance
from our God of loyal love, Jehovah.
First, in the Scriptures, what is endurance?
Well, the Greek noun denotes
“courageous, steadfast, or patient ‘endurance’
“that does not lose hope in the face of obstacles, persecutions,
trials, or temptations.”
It’s a beautiful quality.
The related verb often has the sense
of remaining instead of fleeing,
standing one’s ground, persevering.
Organized to Do Jehovah’s Will in chapter 17
gives a beautiful description of this quality.
You may wish to read it later, but it pointedly states this in one sentence:
“Without endurance, we cannot stay in the truth.”
Well, why is endurance
—this beautiful, precious quality that we need to continue cultivating—
so important for all of us,
regardless of how many years we’ve been running in the race?
Well, think of an illustration.
Think of literal runners in a marathon.
At the start, all of the runners worked hard to qualify.
That’s excellent.
But what happens to a runner who gives up
anywhere before crossing the finish line?
Is he any better than a person who gave up
much earlier in the race
or a person who didn’t even try to join the race?
No.
The results for tiring out or giving up are the same
—disqualification.
We would lose out on the reward.
Well, what’s the point?
All of us —regardless of how long we’ve been running,
regardless of how tired we may be right now—
need to be determined to run to the finish
with Jehovah’s help.
You know, this thought reminded me of a comment
that I heard from Brother Mancoca.
If you’ve read the theocratic history of Angola
in the Yearbook,
then you’ve read about Brother João Mancoca.
His faithfulness during periods of intense persecution
is something we all wish to imitate.
Brother Mancoca is still alive.
He’s 95 years of age.
He’s a faithful and energetic brother
supporting the Branch Committee there in Angola.
Several years ago, we had the privilege of meeting him
when he was 88 years of age.
I was giving him an encouraging visit,
but it turned out to be much more encouraging for me, I’m sure,
than it was for him.
In discussing his past faithfulness, it was interesting his comment.
He said this.
He said, “It’s not what I was that matters;
it’s who I am that matters.”
Yes, Brother Mancoca and you dear elderly brothers and sisters
who are in the race and who have been in the race,
you understand endurance.
You know that it means striving forward, moving forward,
maintaining a strong hope and a positive view,
no matter how many the trials or how difficult they are.
Well, that’s our goal—isn’t it?— all of us, to endure to the end.
I invite you now to open up your Bible with me
to 1 Corinthians 10:13.
Here we find a very comforting assurance.
We’ve read it before.
But as we discuss it and analyze it for just a few moments,
I’d like you to think about it not only for yourself,
but think about someone in your family or in your congregation
who would benefit by having this reminder shared with them.
And perhaps during the weeks to come,
we can think about others
who need the encouragement that this scripture provides.
First Corinthians 10:13 —it reads:
“No temptation has come upon you
“except what is common to men.
“But God is faithful,
“and he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear,
“but along with the temptation he will also make the way out
so that you may be able to endure it.”
Well, how would you summarize the assurance given in God’s inspired Word?
It’s this:
No matter what trials may yet arise in our life
before we get to the finish line,
Jehovah will sustain us if we trust in him.
We might notice in the reading two fundamental truths
that serve as the foundation for this comfort.
First, did you notice in the beginning part of verse 13,
it says that the trials we face are “common to men”?
What does that mean?
Well, that means that anything we’re going through now
—stresses, anxieties, difficulties—
is common to the human experience.
As a result, they’re not beyond our capacity to bear up
as long as we rely on Jehovah God.
In the context of these words in 1 Corinthians chapter 10,
particularly in verses 6 to 11,
we note that Paul refers to the tests
that the Israelites faced in the wilderness.
Now, think of the tests they faced.
None of those trials
while walking in a wilderness for 40 years
were beyond human experience
or, in other words, beyond the ability of faithful Israelites
to bear up under.
Interestingly, Paul says four times
that some of them disobeyed.
Yes, sadly, some Israelites gave in to wrong desires,
not because their trials were just too much
for their weak human souls to bear;
nor was it because Jehovah had failed them.
No, it was because some of them failed to rely on God.
What’s the second fundamental truth in this verse?
Well, we read that “God is faithful.”
Well, we know that to be true, don’t we?
Our experience with Jehovah
has proven him to be faithful in supporting us
in all previous tests we’ve faced.
Indeed, the record of God’s dealings with his people
demonstrates that he’s abundant in loyal love
(as we discussed last evening),
abundant in loyal love
to those who obey him.
Like Joshua, we look back at the record
that we’ve experienced with Jehovah
and the record that his people since the time of Israel
have experienced with Jehovah,
and what do we know?
We know with all our heart, with all our soul,
that “not one word
“out of all the good promises that Jehovah . . . has [made] . . .
has failed.”
What does that mean?
Jehovah will be faithful to us today and tomorrow
as we face tests and temptations.
So two points we can take away:
(1) Jehovah will not allow any trial to develop to a point
where it would make it impossible for us to bear
and (2) he will make the way out for us.
Yes, Jehovah, in various ways,
can either remove trials
or help us to endure trials
with joy, with hope, with determination,
so that all of us can, with his help, cross that finish line.
Well, may these thoughts today move us
to run with endurance another day in Jehovah’s service,
and may we be determined to help others to do the same
as we encourage and upbuild one another.

cn.text: 请大家跟我一起打开圣经
我们完整地读一下今天的经文
这是保罗写给提摩太的信
这封信大约是公元65年写的
当时保罗在罗马，他被囚禁
那问题是，在保持忍耐方面
我们先来读一下提摩太后书4:7,8
“那美好的一仗我已经打过了
从现在起，有正义的冠冕留给我
施行正义审判的主会把冠冕赏赐给我
也赐给所有热切盼望他显现的人”
但他还是非常勇敢、非常积极
他保持忍耐为耶和华服务
在马太福音24:13说的话真实可信
（无论是忍耐到自己生命的终结
还是这个事物制度的终结）
像保罗一样，我们也在跑永生的赛程
我们可以问问自己这个问题
而且一天比一天更接近终点
但我们有没有觉得疲惫呢？
坏消息、看到亲朋好友受苦
而在等待这个事物制度终结的时候
为了鼓励大家不要灰心或放弃
我想先跟大家讨论一下
圣经中“忍耐”这个词的含义
大有忠贞之爱的上帝耶和华
首先，在圣经里“忍耐”是什么意思呢？
被译作“忍耐”的希腊语词
即使面对障碍、迫害、考验、引诱
通常指“留下而不是逃跑
《组织起来遵行耶和华的旨意》的第17章
这本书谈到忍耐时说了这样一句话
“我们不忍耐，就无法坚守真理”
为什么我们都需要培养忍耐
这种美好而宝贵的特质呢？
不论我们参加永生的赛程多少年
为什么这个特质对所有人都很重要呢？
请想象参加马拉松比赛的选手
所有的选手都努力符合资格参加比赛
在到达终点前就停下来、放弃了
他比那些在比赛一开始就停下来的人
或者没有参加比赛的人好一些吗？
不论他是跑到哪里放弃的
不管我们参加永生的赛程有多久
也不管我们现在感到有多疲惫
靠着耶和华的帮助跑到终点
我就想起曼科卡弟兄说过的话
如果你阅读《年鉴》里安哥拉的历史
你就能读到若昂·曼科卡弟兄的故事
他在面对猛烈迫害的时候，仍然保持忠贞
是我们所有人学习的榜样
现在，他仍然是安哥拉分部委员会的成员
几年前，我有机会见到曼科卡弟兄
但没想到，我受到的鼓励更多
曼科卡弟兄讲述了自己过去的经历
之后，他说了这样一句话
“重要的不是我以前做了什么
而是我现在是怎样的人”
多年来都一直在跑永生的赛程
你们明白“忍耐”是什么意思
不管你们遇到多少考验
不管这些考验有多么严峻
你们都保持积极的态度
现在请大家跟我一起打开圣经
经文里谈到的这个保证
这节经文我们都很熟悉
请你同时也想一想自己的情况
也请想一想你可以怎样运用这节经文
去鼓励你的家人和会众里的弟兄姐妹
可能在接下来的几个星期
怎样运用这节经文去鼓励别人
不过是其他人也遇到的
他不会让你们受引诱超过你们能忍受的
他会打开出路，让你们忍耐得住”
这节经文给了我们什么样的保证呢？
就是在我们到达终点线之前
不管我们面对什么样的考验
经文在提出安慰之前，指出两个事实
这些都是其他人也会经历的
因此，只要我们信赖耶和华上帝
我们遇到考验时就能承受得住
保罗谈到以色列人在旷野时遇到的考验
他们在旷野流浪40年期间遇到的所有考验
都是人能够承受得了的
换句话说，只要以色列人保持忠心
以色列人不愿意服从上帝
很可惜，有些以色列人向欲望屈膝
这不是因为他们遇到的引诱是人无法抗拒的
也不是因为耶和华没有帮助他们
这都是因为，他们没有信赖耶和华
经文谈到的第二个事实是什么呢？
我们从自己的经历就能看出
他以前帮助过我们克服困难
从耶和华和他子民来往的历史
耶和华都怀有忠贞的厚爱
我们可以像约书亚一样
回顾自己跟耶和华来往的经历
以及耶和华跟以色列人来往的历史
我们就会从“心底里清楚知道”
耶和华承诺赐福给我们
我们遇到考验和引诱的时候
第一，耶和华不会让我们面对的考验
超过我们能够承受的限度
第二，他会为我们打开出路
耶和华可以用很多方法
把我们面对的考验除去
或者他可以帮助我们怀着喜乐、怀着希望
我们靠着他的帮助，就能够跑到终点
愿今天的这个演讲能够帮助你
在为耶和华服务时保持忍耐
愿我们也能帮助别人忍耐到底
